UI_ROGUE_GRAVE_STONE_DESC1:
A memory is burned into this strange material, an echo of another lifetime...

"The leviathan was like nothing I've ever seen.
So vast as to blot out the sun.
I wanted it. I deserve to have it! It will be mine.
But it resisted, would not come quietly.
It wailed and it wailed as the infra-knife carved into its meat.
It almost took me down with it. Perhaps it has. Perhaps..."
UI_ROGUE_GRAVE_STONE_DESC2:
A memory is burned into this strange material, an echo of another lifetime...

"The same nightmare chases me: a wail fills my cockpit, the dashboard controls gummed with blood.
I have given up sleep. I pulse past blurred stars.
And then there it was: majestic, drifting in the ocean of space.
Something inside me burns for it. I must have it.
Its great fin flexed toward my ship, and my hull was gone..."
UI_ROGUE_GRAVE_STONE_DESC3:
A memory is burned into this strange material, an echo of another lifetime...

"Today should have been the day. Their hour was at hand.
It must be mine. They are like nothing I've ever seen.
Everything was prepared. But it moved faster than I thought possible. As though it knew where I would fly, before I knew it myself.
A great tentacle hugged my ship, my cockpit - pressing my suit down to the bone. This suit will be my grave."
UI_ROGUE_GRAVE_STONE_DESC4:
A memory is burned into this strange material, an echo of another lifetime...

"The chase is over, and I have lost.
The giants will endure, and I will end.
As I plummeted from the sky, I saw another ship falling alongside mine. Then another, and another.
I may have imagined it. The misfiring of a dying mind...
Those creatures were so beautiful. But it is all ended now.
They will haunt my thoughts no longer."
UI_ROGUE_GRAVE_STONE_DESC5:
A memory is burned into this strange material, an echo of another lifetime...

"I came face-to-face with a creature more beautiful and bizarre than anything I have ever seen.
Despite no discernible eyes, I do not believe it is blind.
It was huge, glorious, serene. But then - with a flick of its tentacles, it was gone.
I have thought of nothing else since. I can only think of the whale. whale. whale. wail."

* Game Options are easily accessible from the start screens, with new options and improved organisation.
* For a limited time unlock new content including the Fearsome Visor, a Robotic Companion and much more.

UPDATE_19_TITLE: No Man's Sky version 5.0: WORLDS PART I
UPDATE_19_INTRO:
No Man's Sky WORLDS transforms the universe, bringing huge leaps in water and cloud quality, as well as increased planetary variety, new gameplay features, and more!

Worlds Part I represents the first component of the Worlds Update, with even more to come later. For full details please see www.nomanssky.com.
UPDATE_19_BULLET1: BULLETPOINT Total overhaul of water and cloud rendering, as well as other significant quality improvements and optimisations.
UPDATE_19_BULLET2: BULLETPOINT Boosted planetary variety with new biomes, new creatures, colour and lighting changes, and much more.
UPDATE_19_BULLET3: BULLETPOINT New gameplay features, including Solar ship crafting, the Liquidators Expedition, aquatic ship landing, discovery renaming, new hostile creatures and more.
UPDATE_19_BULLET4: BULLETPOINT Additional significant changes will follow later in the year.
UPDATE_19_OUTRO:
WORLDS PART I represents a huge visual leap for No Man's Sky, with even more to come in WORLDS PART II.

Hello Games has been hard at work to improve and expand No Man's Sky. We hope you enjoy. :)

By default, certain UI actions require the interact button to be briefly held to confirm your decision.

You may wish to adjust this setting if holding the interact button causes discomfort.

Lowering this value may make the ship easier to control, but can feel less responsive.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_OPTIONS_CURSOR_SEN_D:

If enabled, during space combat you can use AUTOFOLLOW to have your ship automatically lock on and chase your target, making space combat much simpler to control. You can change targets with with PREVTARGET / NEXTTARGET.

Off - Auto-follow disabled.

On toggle - Pressing AUTOFOLLOW_T once will set your ship to follow your combat target. Pressing a second time will disable following.

Hold - Your ship will continue to follow your combat target while AUTOFOLLOW_H is held, and stop when AUTOFOLLOW_H is released.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%

PC_SETTINGS_WINDOWMODE_FS_D:
Change the display of the game window.

Bordered - Display a window border around the game.

Borderless - Hide the window border.

Fullscreen - Stretch the game window to fill the entire screen. This may slightly improve performance.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_SETTINGS_PRESET_D:
In general, higher visual settings will improve the appearance of the game, but demand more processing power from your system.

If you experience performance issues while playing, such as a slow or inconsistent framerate, try selecting a lower preset, or fine-tune the individual settings below.

Note that some settings will require a restart of the game to take effect.
PC_GRAPHICS_MONITOR_D: Select which monitor to display the game on.
PC_GRAPHICS_RESOLUTION_D:
Select the resolution to display the game at.

Increasing the resolution may reduce game performance.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_RES_SCALE_D:
This value scales the 3D rendering resolution of the game, independently of the UI resolution and the window resolution.

This means UI can render at a higher resolution to the 3D game view, offering more options for improving performance while keeping UI crisp.

Additionally, the in-game resolution may be scaled larger than the actual screen resolution, allowing for greater image quality than possible when rendering at the monitor's native resolution.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_RES_SCALE_ALT_D:
Scales the 3D rendering resolution of the game, independently of the UI resolution and the window resolution.

This means UI can render at a higher resolution to the 3D game view, offering more options for improving performance while keeping UI crisp.

Additionally, the in-game resolution may be scaled larger than the actual screen resolution, allowing for greater image quality.

Note: only compatible with Anti Aliasing options FXAA or Off.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_V_SYNC_D:
V-Sync prevents screen tearing by forcing the game output to refresh in-sync with the display.

Off - V-Sync is always disabled. Input latency is minimised but game will frequently screen tear.

On - V-Sync is always enabled. Frame drops will cause stuttering.

Adaptive - V-Sync is adaptive. Frame drops will cause screen tearing.

Triple Buffered - V-Sync is enabled and stuttering is minimised. Input latency is slightly increased.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_MAX_FPS_D:
The maximum framerate the game will render.

Reducing this value may improve performance or remedy screen tearing and other display issues.

Increasing this value may make the game look smoother.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_ADAPTER_D: Select which GPU the game should use.
PS4_LOCK_FPS_D:

Fixed - The camera uses a standard height regardless of your character's height.

UI_HEAD_BOB_D:

OPTIONS_INVERT_D:

UI_OPTIONS_TRIGGER_STRENGTH_D:

UI_VR_OPTION_MOVEMENT_DIR_D:

World Relative - Pushing forward will move your character in the direction your controller is pointing.

Body Relative - Pushing forward will move your character in the direction their body is pointing.

UI_VR_OPTION_MOVEMENT_DIR_ALT_D:
This setting adjusts how movement input is interpreted in VR.

World Relative - Your character will move in the direction your controller is pointing.

Body Relative - Your character will move in the direction their body is pointing.

Head Relative - Your character will move in the direction your head is pointing.

This setting adjusts how movement input is interpreted in VR.

Body Relative - Pushing forward will move your character in the direction their body is pointing.

GYRO_ENABLED_D: Motion sensor controls can be used in addition to the left and right sticks for fine-tuning your aim.
GYRO_MODE_ONFOOT_D:
Determines the conditions in which to enable motion sensor controls while travelling on foot.

Never - Disables motion sensor controls.

Visor Only - Motion sensor controls are only active while using the Analysis Visor.

Visor and Firing - Motion sensor controls are active while using the Analysis Visor, or firing the Multi-Tool.

Always - Motion sensor controls are always active while travelling on foot

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ALLOW_RIDING_D:

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_MODE_BUILDING_D:
Determines the conditions in which to enable motion sensor controls while building.

Never - Disable motion sensor controls while building.

Placement Only - Motion sensor controls are only enabled while placing objects.

Selection Only - Motion sensor controls are only enabled while selecting objects.

Always - Enable motion sensor controls while building.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_APPLY_BLD_TO_FREE_CAM_D:
Determines whether motion sensor controls are enabled when you launch the free floating Build Camera.

Never - Disable motion sensor controls while using the Build Camera.

Match Build Mode - Inherit the Active Modes While Building setting.

Always - Enable motion sensor controls while using the Build Camera.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_MODE_EXOCRAFT_D:
Determines the conditions in which to enable motion sensor controls while piloting Exocraft.

Never - Disable motion sensor controls while piloting Exocraft.

Firing Only - Motion sensor controls will only be enabled while firing an Exocraft weapon.

Always - Enable motion sensor controls while piloting Exocraft.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_LOOK_STICK_ENABLED_D:
This option determines how motion sensor controls should behave when CAM_LOOK is used.

No Change - If motion sensor controls are currently enabled, motions will continue to affect your camera.

Activate Motion Sensor - When CAM_LOOK is nudged, motion sensor controls are activated, even if they are otherwise disabled in this context. This causes motion sensor input to adjust your CAM_LOOK input.

Deactivate Motion Sensor - When CAM_LOOK is nudged, motion sensor controls are deactivated and only your CAM_LOOK input is used.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_CURSOR_ENABLED_D:
If enabled, the cursor will respond to motion sensor input while navigating menus.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_CURSOR_ENABLED_D_NX:
If enabled, the cursor will respond to motion sensor input while navigating menus.

Note this feature does not apply when playing in handheld mode.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_CURSOR_SENSITIVITY_X_D:
This value, ranging from 1-3, determines the interface cursor's sensitivity to motion sensor input in the horizontal direction while using menus.

Increasing this value will increase the amount the cursor moves in response to motions.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_CURSOR_SENSITIVITY_Y_D:
This value, ranging from 1-3, determines the interface cursor's sensitivity to motion sensor input in the vertical direction while using menus.

Increasing this value will increase the amount the cursor moves in response to motions.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_SENSITIVITY_TIGHT_THRESH_D:
Movements smaller than the given angle threshold, ranging from 0-20 degrees/second, will be slowed down, allowing more fine-grained control when navigating menus.

Set this value to 0 to disable cursor tightening.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_CURSOR_STICK_ENABLED_D:
This option determines how motion sensor controls should behave when FE_CURSOR is used while navigating menus.

No Change - If motion sensor controls are currently enabled, motions will continue to affect your cursor.

Deactivate Motion Sensor - When FE_CURSOR is nudged, motion sensor controls are deactivated and only your FE_CURSOR input is used.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_HANDEDNESS_D: When using multiple Joy-Con controllers, the Joy-Con in the specified hand will be used for motion sensor input.
GYRO_SENSITIVITY_X_D:
This value, ranging from 1-20, determines the camera's sensitivity to motion sensor input in the horizontal direction during gameplay.

A sensitivity of 1 maps directly to real-world values, i.e. moving the motion sensor by 10 degrees in the real world will rotate the camera by 10 degrees in-game.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_SENSITIVITY_Y_D:
This value, ranging from 1-20, determines the camera's sensitivity to motion sensor input in the vertical direction during gameplay.

A sensitivity of 1 maps directly to real-world values, i.e. moving the motion sensor by 10 degrees in the real world will rotate the camera by 10 degrees in-game.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_STEADYING_D:
Movements smaller than the given angle, ranging from 0-10, will be smoothed out and slowed down, allowing small movements to be used for more precise control. 

Reduce this value to 0 to disable steadying.

This setting combines multiple advanced options: smoothing, tightening and vibration filtering. 

If advanced motion sensor options are enabled, this setting is ignored.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ACCELERATION_D:
This value, ranging from 1-10, applies a multiplier to the cursor's speed when making large motion sensor input in menus.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ADVANCED_D:
Activate advanced motion sensor options to further fine tune motion sensor input.

Note these settings only apply to gameplay control, and not the menu cursor.
GYRO_SCOPE_MULTIPLIER_D:
This value, ranging from 0-20, applies a multiplier to motion sensor sensitivity while using the Analysis Visor.

Set this value to 1.0 to match the base on-foot sensitivity.

Increase this value above 1 to increase motion sensor sensitivity. Reduce it below 1 to reduce motion sensor sensitivity.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_AIMING_MULTIPLIER_D:
This value, ranging from 0-20, applies a multiplier to motion sensor sensitivity while firing a Multi-Tool.

Set this value to 1.0 to match the base on-foot sensitivity.

Increase this value above 1 to increase motion sensor sensitivity. Reduce it below 1 to reduce motion sensor sensitivity.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_EXOCRAFT_MULTIPLIER_D:
This value, ranging from 0-20, applies a multiplier to motion sensor sensitivity while piloting an Exocraft.

Set this value to 1.0 to match the base on-foot sensitivity. 

Increase this value above 1 to increase motion sensor sensitivity. Reduce it below 1 to reduce motion sensor sensitivity.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_BUILDING_MULTIPLIER_D:
This value, ranging from 0-20, applies a multiplier to motion sensor sensitivity while building.

Set this value to 1.0 to match the base on-foot sensitivity. 

Increase this value above 1 to increase motion sensor sensitivity. Reduce it below 1 to reduce motion sensor sensitivity.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ZOOM_SCALE_SENSITIVITY_D:
If enabled, your motion sensor sensitivity will be reduced as your camera zooms in.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ROTATION_SPACE_D:
Determines the point of reference used for motion sensor rotations.

Local - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to the controller.

Player - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to your body in physical space.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ROTATION_SPACE_D_NX:
Determines the point of reference used for motion sensor rotations.

Local - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to the Joy-Con controllers or Pro Controller.

Player - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to your body in physical space.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ROTATION_SPACE_HANDHELD_D:
Determines the point of reference used for motion sensor rotations while playing in handheld mode.

Local - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to the Nintendo Switch.

Player - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to your body in physical space.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_YAW_AXIS_D: This setting allows you to invert or ignore Yaw (left-right) axis movement.
GYRO_ROLL_AXIS_D: This setting allows you to invert or ignore Roll (clockwise-anticlockwise) axis movement.
GYRO_PITCH_AXIS_D: This setting allows you to invert or ignore Pitch (up-down) axis movement.
GYRO_SMOOTHING_THRESHOLD_D:
Movements smaller than the given angle, ranging from 0-20, will be averaged, smoothing them out. This may make it easier to make stable movements.

Reduce this value to 0 to disable smoothing.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_SMOOTHING_WINDOW_D:
This value, ranging from 0-20, represents the time window for applying smoothing to motion sensor movements.

Decreasing this value can make motion sensor movements feel more immediately responsive.

Increasing this value can make motion sensor movements feel smoother, but carry "momentum" for longer.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_TIGHTENING_THRESHOLD_D:
Movements smaller than the given angle, ranging from 0-20, will be slowed down for more precise control.

Reduce this value to 0 to disable tightening.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_DEADZONE_D:
Movements smaller than the given angle, ranging from 0-20, are ignored entirely, reducing any shake from unintended incidental movements.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_FILTER_VIBRATION_D:
If enabled, motion sensor movement resulting from controller vibrations will be ignored.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_FILTER_VIBRATION_D_NX:
If enabled, motion sensor movement resulting from Joy-Con or Pro Controller vibrations will be ignored.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
GYRO_ENABLED_STEAM_D: Determines whether native motion sensor inputs are enabled during gameplay with supported controllers.
GYRO_ENABLED_STMDCK: Native Motion Sensor in Gameplay (Steam Deck)
GYRO_ENABLED_STMDCK_D: Determines whether native motion sensor inputs are enabled for controlling gameplay directly with the Steam Deck (when no external controllers are used).
GYRO_CURSOR_ENABLED_STEAM: Native Motion Sensor Cursor in Menus
GYRO_CURSOR_ENABLED_STEAM_D:
If enabled, the cursor will respond to motion sensor input while navigating menus.

This feature is not available on the Steam Deck when no external controllers are used.
GYRO_ROTATION_SPACE_STMDCK_D:
Determines the point of reference used for motion sensor rotations while playing on Steam Deck without an external controller.

Local - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to the Steam Deck.

Player - Motion sensor rotation is considered relative to your body in physical space.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_UNSTUCK_FREIGHTER_DESC: While onboard a freighter, this button can be used to perform an emergency warp and reset to a safe location. Only recommended in cases of being trapped in the hull or base construction area.
UI_DOMINANT_HAND_D:
Switches which hand the Multi-Tool is held in.

While playing with a third person camera, this also switches which side of the screen the character appears on.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_ROTATE_CAMERA_D:
This setting adjusts the third person camera behaviour while travelling on foot.

Follow - While moving, the camera will automatically smoothly rotate to follow the player if there have been no manual camera adjustments for some time.

Manual - While moving, the camera will never rotate unless manually adjusted by the player.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_MULTIPLAYER_D:
If enabled, you may encounter other players as you explore the universe. This will be most noticeable in high traffic areas, such as the Space Anomaly.

Even if multiplayer is disabled, players will still be able to join your group if you invite them.
UI_PRIV_JOIN_LOBBY_D:
Determines which other players, if any, can join your multiplayer group without invitation.

Regardless of this setting, if multiplayer is enabled, you may still encounter other players.
UI_NETWORK_VOICE_SWITCH_D: If enabled, you will be able to hear voice chat from other players in your multiplayer session, and they will be able to hear you.
UI_PRIV_TEXT_CHAT_D: If enabled, you will see text chat messages sent by other players in your multiplayer session, and they will be able to see yours.
UI_PRIV_DAMAGE_D: Determines which other players, if any, can deal damage to and receive damage from you in multiplayer.
UI_PRIV_ADD_PARTS_D: Determines which other players, if any, can add parts to a base you own.
UI_PRIV_DELETE_PARTS_D: Determines which other players, if any, can remove parts from a base you own.
UI_PRIV_SEE_SHIP_D:
While in multiplayer you can choose to indicate to other players where you are while piloting a ship.

This can make it much easier to meet up with other players. You may wish to disable the marker, or limit who sees it, if you wish to avoid encounters with others.
UI_PRIV_SEE_PLAYER_D:
While in multiplayer you can choose to indicate to other players where you are while travelling on foot.

This can make it much easier to meet up with other players. You may wish to disable the marker, or limit who sees it, if you wish to avoid encounters with others.
UI_PRIV_EDIT_TERRAIN_D: Determines which other players, if any, can edit the terrain around a base you own.
UI_SPEECH_TO_TEXT_D: If enabled, the voice chat of players in your multiplayer session will be converted into text chat.
UI_TRANSLATE_D: If enabled, text chat from players in your multiplayer session will be automatically translated into your language.
UI_PRIV_ACCESS_REFINER_D: Determines which other players, if any, can add and remove items from a refiner you own.

Set this value to 0 to disable headset feedback.

UI_INWORLDCONTROLS_D: If enabled, you must grab onto the in-world steering controls in order to pilot ships and Exocraft.
GYRO_ENABLED_DOCKED_D: Determines whether motion sensor controls are enabled while playing in TV mode or tabletop mode.
GYRO_ENABLED_HANDHELD_D: Determines whether motion sensor controls are enabled while playing in handheld mode.
UI_REVERT_OPTIONS_TEXT: Would you like to reset all options on this page to their default values?
UI_POPUP_RESTART_MSG: Restart required for settings to take effect.
UI_POPUP_GOTO_MODESELECT_MSG: Settings will be applied when returning to Mode Select.
UI_HIGH_RES_VR_UI_D:
Scales and positions user interface elements, such as menus and the HUD, when playing in VR.

Nearer - Brings UI elements closer to your head.

Further - Pushes UI elements further from your head.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_HUD_PLAYER_DIST_D:
This value, a percentage ranging from 20-100, allows you to fine-tune the position of Heads-Up Display (HUD) elements when playing in VR.

Decrease this value to bring HUD elements closer to your head. Increase it to push HUD elements further from your head.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_HUD_COCKPIT_DIST_D:
This value, a percentage ranging from 20-100, allows you to fine-tune the position of Heads-Up Display (HUD) elements when piloting a Ship or Exocraft in VR.

Decrease this value to bring HUD elements closer to your head. Increase it to push HUD elements further from your head.

Note that this value is an offset applied to the base VR HUD Distance value.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_DIALOGUE_SELECT_MODE_D:
Determines how input is handled during text-based interactions such as dialogue with NPCs.

Direct - on-screen buttons are directly highlighted with FE_CURSOR.

Cursor - FE_CURSOR controls a cursor.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_HUD_POSITION_D:
Determines the positioning of Heads-Up Display (HUD) elements when playing in VR.

Head Relative - HUD elements will move as though attached to your head.

Fixed Position - HUD elements will remain fixed to your character's body.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
XBONEX_ENHANCEMENT_D:
Determines whether the game prioritises graphical fidelity and quality or fast performance.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
XBOXSERIESS_ENHANCEMENT_D:
Determines whether the game prioritises graphical fidelity and quality or fast performance.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_CONTROLLER_CURSOR: Motion Sensor Cursor in VR Menus
UI_VR_CONTROLLER_CURSOR_D:
If enabled, the cursor will respond to motion sensor input while navigating menus in VR.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_COMPLEXITY_WARNING_D:
By default, the number of base parts visible at the same time is limited to ensure stability and smooth performance.

Warning: Disabling this setting may have a negative impact on performance when viewing large bases.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_BUILD_GHOSTS_D:
When constructing a base, available placement options for your selected base part are represented with translucent previews of the part. This setting adjusts where these previews appear when building in VR.

Head Relative - As you look around, base part previews will appear where your head is pointing.

Controller Relative - As you move your hands, base part previews will appear where your controller is pointing.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_WRIST_MENU_MOVING_D:
When playing in VR, certain menus, such as the Exosuit and Multi-Tool Inventory, are accessible via projected in-world interfaces.

This option will allow you to grab these wrist projector menus with INTERACT or INTERACT_LEFT, and reposition them to attach to a different point around your hand or Multi-Tool.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_GRAPHICS_ANTI_ALIASING_MAC_D:
Anti aliasing uses various techniques to smooth out jagged edges around objects (which appear as a result of square pixels forming non-rectangular shapes).

MSAA - Multisample Anti-Aliasing (MSAA) is an optimised variation of supersampling that smoothes 'jaggies' appearing at the intersection of two triangles.

MetalFX Spatial - MetalFX Spatial upscaling provides high image quality with improved framerates.

MetalFX Temporal - MetalFX Temporal upscaling uses information from multiple frames to provide the best image quality at a higher computational cost than Spatial upscaling.

This setting only affects GPU performance.
UI_GRAPHICS_AA_MAC_INTELBASED:
Anti aliasing uses various techniques to smooth out jagged edges around objects (which appear as a result of square pixels forming non-rectangular shapes).

MSAA - Multisample Anti-Aliasing (MSAA) is an optimised variation of supersampling that smoothes 'jaggies' appearing at the intersection of two triangles.

MetalFX Spatial - MetalFX Spatial upscaling provides high image quality with improved framerates.

This setting only affects GPU performance.
UI_GRAPHICS_AA_MAC_MONTEREY:
Anti aliasing uses various techniques to smooth out jagged edges around objects (which appear as a result of square pixels forming non-rectangular shapes).

MSAA - Multisample Anti-Aliasing (MSAA) is an optimised variation of supersampling that smoothes 'jaggies' appearing at the intersection of two triangles.

This setting only affects GPU performance.
UI_GRAPHICS_RES_SCALE_MAC_D:
Scales the 3D rendering resolution of the game, independently of the UI resolution and the window resolution.

This means UI can render at a higher resolution to the 3D game view, offering more options for improving performance while keeping UI crisp.

Additionally, the in-game resolution may be scaled larger than the actual screen resolution, allowing for greater image quality.

Note: not compatible with FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0, or MetalFX Upscaling.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_DRS_LOWER_BOUND_D:
Dynamic resolution scaling (DRS) is a technique where the rendering resolution adapts in real time to maintain a more consistent framerate, and improve visual quality in situations of reduced GPU load.

This setting determines the minimum resolution scale the game is allowed to drop to. Increase this value to 1.0 to disable DRS entirely.

Note that DRS is only compatible with some Anti Aliasing settings.

This setting only affects GPU performance.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_DRS_AGGRESSIVENESS_D:
Dynamic resolution scaling (DRS) aggressiveness controls how responsive the game is in dropping the rendering resolution in order to maintain the framerate defined by the Max FPS setting.

Moderate - For a higher fidelity experience, a higher rendering resolution is preferred, at the cost of a risk of more frequent framerate drops.

Balanced - An optimal rendering resolution is maintained with a moderate risk of framerate drops in certain scenarios.

Aggressive - For the smoothest experience, additional GPU headroom is provided, at the expense of a lowered average rendering resolution.

This setting only affects GPU performance.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_DRS_AGGRESSIVENESS_VR_D:
Dynamic resolution scaling (DRS) aggressiveness controls how responsive the game is in dropping the rendering resolution in order to maintain the framerate matching your VR headset display frequency.

Moderate - For a higher fidelity experience, a higher rendering resolution is preferred, at the cost of a risk of more frequent framerate drops.

Balanced - An optimal rendering resolution is maintained with a moderate risk of framerate drops in certain scenarios.

Aggressive - For the smoothest experience, additional GPU headroom is provided, at the expense of a lowered average rendering resolution.

This setting only affects GPU performance.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_FLIGHT_STICK_ROLL_D:
While playing in VR using motion controls, the starship is piloted by grabbing and moving the in-world stick in the cockpit.

This setting determines whether the ship will turn (on the "yaw" axis), or roll when moving the ship stick left and right.

Stick Turns Ship - The in-world stick will turn the ship on the yaw axis. ROLLLEFT / ROLLRIGHT, and stick twist (if enabled), will roll the ship.

Stick Rolls Ship - The in-world stick will roll the ship. ROLLLEFT / ROLLRIGHT, and stick twist (if enabled), will turn the ship on the yaw axis.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_FLIGHT_STICK_TWIST_D:
While playing in VR using motion controls, the starship is piloted by grabbing and moving the in-world stick in the cockpit.

Enabling this setting will allow the ship stick to be twisted, to provide motion control over an additional axis of movement.
Twist / spin the top of the stick while maintaining it in an upright position to move in a single axis, or pull and twist it simultaneously to move in multiple axes at once.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_VR_HIGHLIGHT_INTERACTION_D:
While playing in VR, looking at objects that can be interacted with will highlight them.

Disabling this setting will disable the highlight effect.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_DLSSFRAMEGEN_D:
Frame Generation boosts frame rates by using AI to render additional frames.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_DLSSFRAMEGEN_GHSD_D:
Frame Generation boosts frame rates by using AI to render additional frames.

Enable Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling in the operating system to use Frame Generation.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_DLSSFRAMEGEN_DOOD_D:
Frame Generation boosts frame rates by using AI to render additional frames.

Graphics driver update required to enable Frame Generation.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_NVIDIALOWLATENCY_D:
NVIDIA Reflex reduces system latency and increases PC responsiveness.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
PC_GRAPHICS_NVIDIALOWLAT_FG_D:
NVIDIA Reflex reduces system latency and increases PC responsiveness.

This option is automatically enabled if Frame Generation is on.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%

An exclusive piece of self-adhesive, crease-proof wall art.
This poster represents fragments of many long-distance communication signals between the dominant factions of the universe.

UI_FIREWORK_PACK_TWIT_07_DESC:
A three-pack of flesh launchers.These organic pyrotechnics rocket into the sky and explode in a splatter of slime, plasma and wormlets. Ignite to create disgusting displays in the sky.

Place launch tube via the Build Menu (BUILD_MENU). Warning: Aim away from living creatures. Not recommended for indoor use.
UI_FIREWORK_PROD_SWIRL_P_DESC:
This exotic firework, sparkling with Atlantideum and antimony elements, bursts into a cluster of wildly spiralling ribbons. Ignite to create glittering displays in the sky.

Place launch tube via the Build Menu (BUILD_MENU). Warning: Aim away from living creatures. Not recommended for indoor use.
UI_FIREWORK_PROD_SWIRL_B_DESC:
This exotic firework, sparkling with indium and antimony elements, bursts into a cluster of wildly spiralling ribbons. Ignite to create glittering displays in the sky.

Place launch tube via the Build Menu (BUILD_MENU). Warning: Aim away from living creatures. Not recommended for indoor use.
UI_FIREWORK_PROD_SWIRL_T_DESC:

Place launch tube via the Build Menu (BUILD_MENU). Warning: Aim away from living creatures. Not recommended for indoor use.
BLD_STATION_PART_DESC:
A decorative part designed for use in habitable bases.

This component has been fabricated in the style of one of the universe's many Space Stations.
FOOD_R_HORROR_DESC:
The char of the Nutrient Processor's highest power setting has burned the stench from this one rancid slab. They writh no more...

Can be consumed as it stands or subjected to further processing.
FOOD_HORROR_MEAT_DESC:
A writhing slab of meat, harvested from the corpse of the biological horror that once contained it.

Process in a Nutrient Processor to generate edible products.
UI_WATER_LANDER_DESC:
An advanced upgrade for the starship's landing system, enabling the ship to land and take off from aquatic surfaces.

A mixture of bespoke jets and re-directed exhaust fans allow the ship to hover just above the water's surface.
UI_WATERLAND_ALIEN_DESC:
A salty membrane encases the ship, dramatically increasing its natural buoyancy.

The carapace will allow the vessel to float, making water landings possible.
UI_MECH_FLAME_DESC:
A mounted flamethrower specifically designed for the Minotaur Heavy Exosuit Hybrid. Causes extreme damage at close range.

Use CYCLEWEAPON to cycle available weapon modes.
UI_GRUB_POD_DESC:
This pupa, pulsating and warm, has begun its transformation from throbbing sac of mucus into an unspeakably vile insectoid.

Theoretically processable in a Nutrient Processor to generate edible products.

WARNING: grub-sac will release powerful pheromones if violated.
UP_MECHFLAME2_DESC:
A significant upgrade for all Minotaur Flamethrower Units. Use FE_ALT1 to begin upgrade installation process.

The module is flexible, and exact upgrade statistics are unknown until installation is complete.

Potential improvements include: damage output, burn time and fuel efficiency.
UP_MECHFLAME3_DESC:

The module is flexible, and exact upgrade statistics are unknown until installation is complete.

UI_TRACK_BLACKHOLE_DESC: Nada and Polo have promised to help me as I explore the galaxy. They have marked a black hole for me on my map, and even seem excited that I visit it and see where it takes me...
UI_TRACK_BLACKHOLE_OBJ_TIP:

Travelling through the heart of the black hole allows for rapid progress across the universe, though may cause damage to starship technologies.

A Space Station Teleporter can be used to return to local space if gravitational travel provides an unexpected destination...

UI_ATLAS_LOOP_DESC: I have followed the Atlas across the galaxy, tracing the links between each interface and every seed. And yet, I am still not free of the crimson light that lurks, ever-present, at the edges my vision.
UI_ATLAS_LOOP_OBJ1A: Find a wonder to show the Atlas
UI_ATLAS_LOOP_OBJ1A_TIP:
The Atlas has created infinite stars, infinite worlds, infinite life. But even among infinity, each moment still has meaning. Any atom may seed a new universe.

Find an Atlas Interface and present a wonder. Wonders are a record of your discoveries and can be found in the Catalogue.
UI_ATLAS_LOOP_DESC_A:
The Atlas has created infinite stars, infinite worlds, infinite life. I cannot see them all, nor even truly begin to understand the multitude of existence.
But perhaps even among these endless wonders, each moment can still have meaning. Any atom may seed a new universe, if viewed the right way...
UI_ATLAS_LOOP_RES_A1:
I present the Atlas what I discovered about the planet %DISCO%. It shudders in response, as if the fabric of spacetime were to sigh.
Somewhere out in the beyond, a new star is born, seeded by what I have seen...
UI_ATLAS_LOOP_RES_A2:
I present the Atlas with %DISCO%, a creature I found on the planet %PLANET%. It shimmers in response, the entire interface vibrating as it observes this creature through my eyes.
Somewhere out in the beyond, a new star is born, seeded by what I have seen...
UI_ATLAS_LOOP_RES_A3:
I present the Atlas with %DISCO%, a plant I discovered on the planet %PLANET%. As I transmit the data, I feel the crimson heartbeat of the station slow to calm and considerate cadence.
And then - a rapid thudding, a staccato echo that fills my entire being. Somewhere out in the beyond, a new star is born, seeded by what I have seen...

The Mark of the Denier surges with power, proof of my journey through the stars, a journey entirely of my own volition.

The strength of the mark - of its denial - can be re-affirmed at an Atlas interface...

UI_ATLAS_LOOP_DESC_B:
At the last, when the Atlas asked me for its final input, I had walked away. It led me down path after path, made me a constant source of data, a part of its endless algorithm. I refused to go any further.
And yet, I find myself standing before it once more. What do I want to prove? That I still have the strength to make my own way? That I wear the mark of my freedom with pride?
UI_ATLAS_LOOP_RES_B1:
I feel the mark burn as I press it onto the Atlas interface. An energy flows through, a crimson magnetism that drags me inwards...
...
I pull away. I have passed my own test.

UI_SAVE_SUMMARY_ATLAS: In the presence of the Atlas
UI_TITLE_OWNED_ATLASDENY: Refused the call of the Atlas
FINAL_U3ATLAS_DENY_DESC_1:
I have barely begun to formulate this heresy within my mind when I feel the response, the tidal swell of crimson light that begins to rise behind my eyes.
The Atlas is all creation, all the purpose in this universe. It calls for progress. It calls for me. Who am I to deny such a force?
FINAL_U3ATLAS_DENY_RES_A:
I leave, the Atlas, alone, abandoned.
I feel it begin to scream, a silent shriek that echoes across all of space and time...
DENIER_ITEM_DESC:
A tiny mote of stardust, no more than a speck. On closer examination, its surface is all crystalline shards and distorted crimson geometry.

It flickers with pent-up energy, demanding to be free.

Empower the mark as you discover systems, planets and objects across the universe.

Return to the planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system, and notify %NAME% of your success to claim your reward.

Completing missions for lifeforms will increase your standing and earn lucrative rewards.

%NAME% claims their facility on planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system is subject to constant pirate harassment. They offer a substantial reward to any who might bring this bombardment to an end.

%PP_SENTENCES%

Use your ship to engage the attackers in combat.

UI_PP_SCAN_CRE_DESC:
%NAME% requires detailed scans of creatures, preferably those who live on their home planet of %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They have not been clear as to what they will do with this data. However, they have made it very clear that I will be rewarded handsomely should I assist them in collecting the data.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_SCAN_CRE_OBJ_TIP:
%NAME% has requested creature scan data.
In the Analysis Visor (AIM), target creatures and hold BINOCSCAN to analyse.
Undiscovered species are indicated in the Visor by red dots.
Track the commonness of creatures, and how many you have discovered, via the Discoveries Page.
UI_PP_SCAN_MIN_DESC:
%NAME% requires geological data. They desire probes of the minerals that litter their home planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system, though will also accept remote scans with sufficient metadata. Despite the translation issues, one thing is clear: there is a substantial reward on offer for any explorer who supplies this data.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_SCAN_MIN_OBJ_TIP:
%NAME% has requested mineral scan data.
In the Analysis Visor (AIM), target rocks and hold BINOCSCAN to analyse.
UI_PP_SCAN_PLA_DESC:
%NAME% is in desperate need of detailed scans of flora - preferably that which grows on their home planet of %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They attempt to explain why, but their meaning is not clear. However, It is apparent that I will be rewarded handsomely should I assist them in collecting the data.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_SCAN_PLA_OBJ_TIP:
%NAME% has requested floral scan data.
In the Analysis Visor (AIM), target plants and hold BINOCSCAN to analyse.
UI_PP_ROBOTS_DESC:
%NAME% seems possessed of a real anger, a hatred towards the Sentinels that swarm across their home planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They offer to to reward me should I find and destroy Sentinel forces.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_ROBOTS_E_OBJ_TIP:
Sentinel Drones patrol most worlds. Engaging the Sentinels will trigger Suppression Measures.
Locate Sentinels with the Analysis Visor, or harvest resources to draw their attention.

See the Combat section of the Guide for further details.
UI_PP_ROBOTS_E_MSG:
Destroy Sentinel Drones: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
Engaging the Sentinels will trigger Suppression Measures
UI_PP_ROBOTS_M_OBJ_TIP:
Sentinel Quads are an advanced combat unit deployed at high alert levels.
Engaging patrolling Drones will trigger Suppression Measures and escalate the alert level.
Locate Sentinels with the Analysis Visor, or harvest resources to draw their attention.

See the Combat section of the Guide for further details.
UI_PP_ROBOTS_M_MSG:
Destroy a Sentinel Quad
Quads are an advanced combat unit deployed at high alert levels
Engage patrolling Drones to trigger Suppression Measures
UI_PP_ROBOTS_H_OBJ_TIP:
Sentinel Mechs are an advanced combat unit deployed at high alert levels.
Engaging patrolling Drones will trigger Suppression Measures and escalate the alert level.
Locate Sentinels with the Analysis Visor, or harvest resources to draw their attention.

See the Combat section of the Guide for further details.
UI_PP_ROBOTS_H_MSG:
Destroy a Sentinel Mech
Mechs are an advanced combat unit deployed at high alert levels
Engage patrolling Drones to trigger Suppression Measures
UI_PP_ROBOTS_C_DESC:
%NAME% of planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system speaks spitefully of the corruption spreading across their home world. Perhaps their anger masks an underlying fear. They offer to to reward me should I find and destroy corrupted Sentinel forces.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_ROBOTS_C_OBJ_TIP:
Corrupt Drones patrol dissonant worlds, their shells warped by a power emanating from the fabric of the planet. Locate dissonant systems in the Galaxy Map. Scan individual planets in space with the starship's scanner (SCAN) to locate worlds with corrupted Sentinel forces.

See the Combat section of the Guide for further details.
UI_PP_KILL_CRE_DESC:
%NAME% seems bored, tired of their life locked away inside their outpost on %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They mention something about the smell of mordite. They appear to want me to hunt for them, and offer a substantial reward should I venture out and kill the creatures that roam this world.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_KILL_CRE_OBJ_TIP:
Locate creatures on a planet's surface.
Within the Analysis Visor (AIM), creatures can be identified by green pawprints or red dots.

Fire the Multi-Tool with ATTACK.
UI_PP_KILL_PRE_DESC:
%NAME% seems to have a distaste towards the predatory creatures that roam their home world of %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. It is unclear whether fear or a different motive drives them, but they assure me of reward should I cull a number of the predators that inhabit this world.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_KILL_PRE_OBJ_TIP:
Locate predatory creatures on a planet's surface. Your suit will mark nearby predators with red icons.
Take care when approaching predators; explorers are a food source for many creatures.
Within the Analysis Visor (AIM), creatures can be identified by green pawprints or red dots.

Fire the Multi-Tool with ATTACK.
UI_PP_KILL_FIE_DESC:
%NAME% seems afraid, whispering incomprehensible warnings. I am able to understand only enough to know that they think strange monstrosities are stalking their home planet of %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system, and that they will reward me should I find and kill these fiends.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_KILL_FIE_OBJ_TIP:
Locate infestation sites near abandoned buildings.
Whispering Eggs litter these haunted sites. The brood will guard their larvae fiercely. Destroy eggs to alert the swarm.
UI_PP_KILL_WRM_DESC:
%NAME% of planet %PLANET% struggles to articulate what they have witnessed on a neighbouring world in the %SYSTEM% system. They stammer about titanic worms, wretched offspring, slavering mouths. They offer recompense to any explorer who dares hunt and cleanse these hungering tendrils.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_KILL_WRM_OBJ_TIP:
The vessel of the many mouths is drawn to Titan Worm Burrows.
Eliminate their Hungering Tendrils to purge the infestation.

Worm Burrows can be located with the Analysis Visor while on infested worlds.
UI_PP_KILL_PLA_DESC:
%NAME% of the %SYSTEM% system seems frustrated. They curse the weeds that strangle their home planet of %PLANET%, muttering about toxic gases and lashing vines. They offer to reward any explorers who could provide a floral extermination service.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_KILL_PLA_OBJ_TIP:
Find Hazardous Flora on the planet surface, or in underground cave systems
Hazardous plants DANGER can be located with the Analysis Visor within a short range

UI_PP_KILL_WRM_MSG5:
Eliminate Hungering Tendrils: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
Scan planets from starship (SCAN) to locate infested worlds
UI_PP_FEED_CRE_DESC:
%NAME% of planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system speaks of their love of the outside world, of how it pains them to be bound to their facility. They relate an elaborate tale of a creature that I gather was once their pet. They seem to be offering a large reward should I wander the planet and feed any wild animals I come across.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_FEED_CRE_OBJ_TIP:
Feed wildlife with Creature Pellets.
Locate creatures using the Analysis Visor (AIM).
Within the Analysis Visor (AIM), creatures can be identified by green pawprints or red dots.
Fed creatures can be ridden, farmed, or adopted as a companion.
UI_PP_DIG_DESC:
%NAME% excitedly informs me of an ancient ruin on planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They share their data, the clue that put them on the trail of this site. They say I may keep any excavated artifacts for myself, as long as I log any important historical discoveries in their name.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_METAL_DESC:
%NAME% of planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system seems agitated, in great need of a particular substance. For reasons I do not understand, they are unable to collect it for themself. They offer a generous reward should I mine a supply on their behalf and return it to their outpost.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_METAL_OBJ_TIP:
Large deposits of metal can be found nearby on planet %PLANET%. Locate these deposits with the Analysis Visor (SCAN).

These deposits will require a Terrain Manipulator to mine.
UI_PP_HARVEST_DESC:
%NAME% of planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system seems agitated, in great need of a particular native plant. For reasons I do not understand, they are unable to collect it for themself. They offer a generous reward should I harvest a supply on their behalf and return it to their outpost.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_HARVEST_OBJ_TIP:
Large patches of wild flora can be found growing nearby on planet %PLANET%. Locate these deposits with the Analysis Visor (SCAN).

This wild flora will require a Hazmat Gauntlet to harvest.

UI_PP_STORM_DESC:
%NAME% has long admired the brilliant crystals that form on their planet of %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. However, they do not themself possess the equipment to gather these during extreme weather, and offer a reward to any explorers who collect storm crystals on their behalf.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_STORM_OBJ_TIP:
Storm Crystals can only be collected during a storm.
Storms place additional stress on Exosuit Hazard Protection systems, and are thus highly dangerous.

UI_PP_BONES_DESC:
%NAME% tells me of natural burial grounds across their home planet of %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. Owing to translation issues, their interest in creature skeletons remains a mystery to me - but I do understand that they would offer compensation for any ancient bones I return to them.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_BONES_OBJ_TIP:
Locate Fossil Beds using the Analysis Visor (AIM).
Use the Terrain Manipulator (ATTACK) to exhume ancient bones.
Beware Living Stone guardians who may awaken to defend these ancient resting grounds...

UI_PP_CORRUPT_PILLARS_DESC:
%NAME% speaks resentfully of the devices boring into their home planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They offer to reward any explorer who helps destroy Dissonance Resonators, claiming that the Sentinels who plague this dissonant world utilise the machinery for malevolent purposes.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_CORRUPT_PILLARS_OBJ_TIP:
The corrupted Sentinel swarm fuel themselves with energy harvested from the fabric of reality itself. Their foul machinery must be destroyed before it corrupts this planet entirely.

Dissonance Resonators can be located with the Analysis Visor while on dissonant worlds.
UI_PP_CORRUPT_PILLARS_MSG2:
Destroy Dissonance Resonators: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
The corrupted swarm feed on disharmonic energy
Locate dissonant extractors with the Analysis Visor (AIM)

Destroy Dissonance Resonators: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
No dissonance detected on local planet
Return to planet %PLANET%

Destroy Dissonance Resonators: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
No dissonance detected in local system
Return to the %SYSTEM% system
UI_PP_CORRUPT_PILLARS_MSG5:
Destroy Dissonance Resonators: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
Scan planets from starship (SCAN) to locate dissonant worlds
UI_PP_PHO_CRE_DESC:
%NAME% enthusiastically describes the creatures inhabiting their planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They lament that their facility is ill-suited to pets, and offer to pay for wildlife photography to decorate their home.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_PHO_CRE_OBJ_TIP:
Locate creatures on a planet's surface.
Within the Analysis Visor (AIM), creatures can be identified by green pawprints or red dots.

Activate Photo Mode with QUICK_MENU.
UI_PP_PHO_CRE_MSG:
Take a photo of %AMOUNT% land-dwelling creatures
Activate photo mode with QUICK_MENU
UI_PP_FACTORY_DESC:
%NAME% of planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system talks in serious tones, pointing out a nearby factory. They claim the installation is malfunctioning, and they wish it restored in exchange for a substantial reward - though warn that Sentinels may respond with force.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_FACTORY_OBJ_TIP:
Gain access to the facility and restore normal operations.
The facility may be secured. Destroy locked doors with Multi-Tool weaponry.
Damaging facilities may attract Sentinel attention.
UI_PP_DEPOT_DESC:
%NAME% babbles a set of coordinates, pointing at a map of their planet %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system. They have identified a resource depot. For reasons I do not understand, they seem excited at the prospect of this depot being destroyed, and offer a generous payment should I bring about this destruction.

%PP_SENTENCES%
UI_PP_DEPOT_OBJ_TIP:
Destroy depots with Multi-Tool or Starship weaponry.
WARNING: Sentinels will respond to aggression with extreme hostility.
UI_PP_DEPOT_MSG:
Find and destroy resource depots: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
%NAME% has provided approximate coordinates
UI_PP_DEPOT_MSG_WEAPON:
Find and destroy resource depots: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%
Construct a Boltcaster in your Multi-Tool
UI_PP_DEPOT_MSG_WEAPON_MODE:
Find and destroy resource depots: %CURRENT%/%AMOUNT%

UI_PP_TRA_DESC_MOOD_1: When pressed for further information, the Gek only smiles.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_MOOD_1: Duty dictates the Vy'keen cannot themself abandon their station.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_MOOD_1: The Korvax does not seem wholly convinced of my capabilities.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_LUSH_1: The Gek regrets they cannot explore this picturesque world themself.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_LUSH_1: The Vy'keen regrets they cannot explore this picturesque world themself.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_LUSH_1: The Korvax regrets they cannot explore this picturesque world themself.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_TOX_1: The Gek coughs delicately, as though the toxic atmosphere troubles them.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_TOX_1: The Vy'keen bears scars from the toxic rain that drenches this world.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_TOX_1: The Korvax's shell is streaked with corrosion from previous expeditions.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_HOT_1: The Gek seems relaxed in their relatively cool facility.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_HOT_1: The Vy'keen's facial tendrils wave, cooling themself.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_HOT_1: An internal cooling system buzzes audibly from within the Korvax's shell.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_RAD_1: The Gek's eyes seem to glow, mirroring the radioactive landscape.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_RAD_1: The Vy'keen draws themself up, their body wearied by this radioactive world.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_RAD_1: Something crackles in the Korvax's shell.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_COLD_1: The Gek shivers as they contemplate the frigid landscape.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_COLD_1: The Vy'keen bristles as they contemplate the frigid landscape.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_COLD_1: The Korvax's visor shimmers as they contemplate the frigid landscape.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_DUST_1: Despite the shelter of their facility, the Gek's leathery skin seems parched.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_DUST_1: The Vy'keen's eyes appear reddened with dehydration.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_DUST_1: Persistent grains of dust scrape in the crevices of the Korvax's shell.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_SWAMP_1: The Gek wipes a pungent drop of sweat from their brow.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_SWAMP_1: The Vy'keen grunts as sweat trickles down their brow.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_SWAMP_1: The Korvax rattles their carapace, dislodging a few drops of condensation.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_B_1: A persuasive scent floods the air.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_B_1: Despite their intimidating appearance, there is a humility to their request.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_B_2: They nod encouragingly, almost pushing me out the door.
UI_PP_WAR_DESC_B_2: They regard me with gravity, withholding judgement for now.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_B_2: Only a fragment of their attention is upon me.
UI_PP_TRA_DESC_B_3: Their small body vibrates with an infectious enthusiasm.
UI_PP_EXP_DESC_B_3: They have already calculated the probability of my success.
UI_PP_CS_DONE_MSG:
Return to the crash site
Find %NAME% near their broken starship
UI_PP_CS_BOUNTY_DESC:
%NAME%'s starship on %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system is in a state of disrepair, rendering them land-bound and stranded.

They claim this predicament was brought about by a pirate attack, and offer a share of their valuable cargo to any who can bring justice to the outlaws.
UI_PP_CS_RAID_DESC:
%NAME%'s starship on %PLANET% in the %SYSTEM% system is in a state of disrepair, rendering them land-bound and stranded.

They claim this predicament was brought about by a vicious attack and theft of their cargo. They were evasive regarding the legitimacy of this cargo, but offer a valuable reward to any who can help retrieve it.
UI_TUTORIAL_SKIPPED_DESC:
I find myself alone on a strange world, unequipped and in danger. I have no memory of how I got here, no sense of a before.

But this ship at least seems to recognise me. The controls react to my touch, or at least to that of my Exosuit.1 I am not dead yet, and this ship is a lifeline out to the stars...
UI_TUTORIAL_SKIPPED_OBJ_TIP:
The galaxy is wide and full of wonder, and it is yours to explore.

While on a planet, you can discover and rename mineral, flora and fauna using the Analysis Visor (AIM), construct a Base using the Build Menu (BUILD_MENU).

Each system has several planets to explore, as well as a Space Station. Use your Starship to visit the station to find a wealth of alien life, as well as upgrades and charts to help planetary exploration.

The Space Anomaly is home to an array of other Travellers. Some will aid you in your journey, forging upgrades from Nanites. Others may ask for your assistance on their own journey.

UI_WIKI_HYPERDRIVE_DESC: Install a Hyperdrive to enable travel to new star systems. Locate and insert all required materials to complete the installation.
UI_WIKI_HYPERDRIVE_OBJ_TIP:
Installing a Hyperdrive will enable interstellar travel.

The Hyperdrive requires Microprocessors and Chromatic Metal.
Microprocessors can be purchased at a Space Station trade terminal. Refine Chromatic Metal from Copper.
UI_WIKI_HYPERFUEL1_DESC:
This antimatter-based fuel is one of the few power sources capable of meeting the incredible energy requirements of a starship hyperdrive.

Craft warp cells from Antimatter and Antimatter Housing. Use PRODMENU to craft in empty Inventory Slots.
UI_WIKI_HYPERFUEL1_OBJ_TIP:
Craft a Warp Cell using Antimatter and Antimatter Housing.

The core components of a warp cell can be gathered on all worlds. A portable refiner is required to process some raw materials into a useable form.

Locate the damaged slot within the Inventory (INVENTORY) and use REPAIR to begin repair process. Primary resource required: Sodium Nitrate.

Sodium Nitrate is most easily created from Sodium in a Refiner. 

Sodium Nitrate is also found in crystal form. Locate sodium nitrate crystals with the Scanner (SCAN). Mining requires use of an Advanced Mining Laser.

UI_EXPED_14_LORE_PREAMBLE:
The terminal has been clogged with a viscous fluid, no doubt some lingering mucus from the brood mother.
Nonetheless, it remains active. The logs of the Liquidator who uncovered this nest are available to read.
UI_EXPED_14_LORE_PREAMBLE2: I sponge the lingering slime from the terminal. The Liquidator's logs are once again available.
UI_EXPED_14_LORE1:
Here follows the testament of Liquidator #3813G of the Vanguard!
...
I was once like you. A mere cleaner, following in the footsteps of the brave Vanguard units who dove into the heart of the vile nests.
I cowered, scared to do my part. Sentinels, broodlings, unspeakable horrors. I thought it would overwhelm me.
And yet - here I am! And like me, you too will rise! You have done your part, and you too will follow the Liquidators to glory!
UI_EXPED_14_LORE2:
Here follows the testament of Liquidator #3813G of the Vanguard!
...
Swarm after swarm exterminated, countless colonies purged. And yet they keep coming, keep growing! They would consume us, were it not for the sacrifices of the Vanguard.
See how the mother protects her grubs! Think what they would do if we left them to multiply in peace!
And so I have marked this nest for you, Liquidator, this hive of vile infestation. If you are reading this, then you have done your part!
UI_EXPED_14_LORE3:
Here follows the testament of Liquidator #3813G of the Vanguard!
...
I have followed this vile brood across planet and moon, from star to star and sector to sector. And now you do too.
I have done what was asked. I have done my part, and now my life and theirs are intertwined. Vanguard and brood, hunter and hunter. A dance to the death...
UI_EXPED_14_LORE4:
Here follows the testament of Liquidator #3813G of the Vanguard!
...
This infestation was stubborn. I had to place the plasma charges by hand, plunging myself into the viscera of the nest.
I did so without fear. I knew those who follow would do their part.
But at its heart, surrounded by grubs, I was submerged in the hive's jelly. It was soft. It was warm. It was a home.
I could not place the charges. I could not do my part.
I am shamed. And now you have done my part for me.
UI_EXPED_14_LORE5:
Here follows the testament of Liquidator #3813G of the Vanguard!
...
I have marked this world for you, but I have not done my part. I leave that to you. You will have done what was asked, I am sure.
From here, I leave my part behind. I am nothing to the Vanguard now, a shameful deserter.

UI_WIKI_SHORT_SALVAGE: Starships and Multi-Tools can be salvaged to earn valuable components and materials. Advanced scrappers can use these materials to build their very own custom starship. Read more...
UI_GUIDE_BODY_SALVAGE:
Starships and Multi-Tools can be salvaged to acquired valuable trade resources as well as inventory and technology upgrades. Salvaging ships or Multi-Tools also frees up additional space for new additions to your collection.

Starships can be salvaged at the Starship Outfitting Terminal found aboard any regular Space Station. Visit the Space Anomaly to salvage your Multi-Tool.

When salvaging a starship, you may instead choose to create a customisation module matching the visuals of part of that ship, typically either its wings, cockpit or engines. These parts can be taken to the Starship Fabricator and assembled into a design of your own choosing.

Purchase a Starship Reactor from a space station technology merchant to determine the statistics and inventory of the resulting ship.

Note: starships built at the Fabricator are not authenticated by the galactic trade authorities and as such are worth less when attempting to trade your ship with another pilot.

UPDATE15_NOTES:
No Man's Sky INTERCEPTOR brings new starships, a new world type, exciting combat and much more. For full details please see www.nomanssky.com.

* Corrupt Sentinel planets - A corruption is spreading. Venture to forsaken Sentinel worlds, harvest strange crystals, and explore abandoned encampments...
* New Starship type - Salvage and claim a Sentinel Interceptor starship for your fleet, a hugely varied new combat craft.
* New enemy type - New corrupted Sentinel machinery take guard, challenging explorers who dare to encroach on their territory.
* Steal Sentinel tech and turn it back against the horde. Including two brand new Multi-Tools, and a unique backpack - the "Aeron Turbojet".
* Curate your own collection of personal records and favourite discoveries in a new addition to the Wonders catalogue.
* A host of combat QOL improvements in space and on planet bring exciting new challenges across the universe.

Hello Games has been hard at work to improve and expand No Man's Sky. We hope you enjoy. :)

Thank you so much,
Hello Games

UI_BACKPACK_SENTINEL_DESC:
An exclusive Exosuit Appearance Override.

A titanium flightpack, assembled from technology stolen from the Sentinel horde. Its engines are precooled with a constant flow of pugneum and nitrogen, ensuring fuel-efficient and deadly silent operation.

Warning: do not unseal pugneum containment chamber without protective gear.

Transform the appearance of your Exosuit at an Appearance Modifier.
UI_FREI_TRAIL_RED_DESC:
An exclusive Freighter Engine Flare Modifier.

A harmonic generation device converts the output of the freighter engines to A T L A S frequencies, radiating a painfully crimson trail.

Transform the appearance of your freighter at the Upgrade Control Terminal on the bridge.
UI_SPEC_HOOD_GEK_DESC:
This grand hood is worn by the upper ranks of Gek at events and conventions, distinguishing the esteemed Trade Lord from the lowly Hireling.

Transform the appearance of your Exosuit with this exclusive Appearance Override at an Appearance Modifier.
UI_LIFESUP_ROBO_DESC:
This device allows a pilot's brain to interface with the mind of the Sentinel Interceptor, granting the pilot access to ship control systems and external sensors.

The enmeshing of the pilot's mind with that of the vessel is necessary to prevent rejection/consumption of the pilot by the ship's vestigial cockpit.
UI_LIFESUP_ROBO_DESC_DAMAGED:
The Sentinel vessel has its own mind, its own way of being. It rejects the control of an outside entity.

It appears there has been a previous attempt to cut out the ship's brain and make its vestigial cockpit habitable, handing control of the ship to a conventional pilot. Complete this installation to claim the ship.
UI_LAUNCHER_ROBO_DESC:
Gently detaches the starship from gravitational fields, lifting it toward the stars.
 
The well hungers for pugneum or radiant shards, and must be sufficiently fueled before launch.
 
Hold THRUST to take off from planet.
Hold BOOST to initiate in-flight speed boost.
UI_SHIPJUMP_ROBO_DESC:
Aligns the ship's electromagnetic emissions with A T L A S waves, providing basic propulsion and Pulse Jump capability.
 
The sub-light drive hungers for tritium or radiant shards.

Hold PULSEJUMP to engage Pulse Jump.
Hold BOOST to initiate in-flight speed boost.
UI_HYPERDRIVE_ROBO_DESC:
A raw optic organ, red and unblinking. Suspended above the ship's engines, it gazes down tunnels in spacetime, allowing FTL travel between star systems.

Direct the core's attention to remote destinations via the Galactic Map.
UI_SHIPSHIELD_ROBO_DESC:
A defensive crimson cocoon, obfuscating the ship's physical form and providing protection from collision and laser fire.

The core self-heals over time, but may be quickly replenished with catalytic elements or radiant shards.
UI_SHIPGUN_ROBO_DESC:
Sentinel-grade weapons system, engineered for the singular purpose of annihilating rogue ships in violation of system regulations.

Press SHIPFIRE to administer lethal force.
UI_DRONE_SALVAGE_DESC:
A pane of watchful g l a s s, retrieved from the smoking remains of the corrupted swarm's Dissonance Resonators. It emits more light than it reflects, casting a faint purple hue on its surroundings.

Highly sought after for salvage operations, as it can be used to bypass the security systems of key Sentinel ship technologies.
UI_DRONE_SHARD_DESC:
A fragment of glassy lifeforce, chipped from a larger formation. Dynamic intermolecular binding gives the shard a strangely flexible, sinewy quality. It writhes gently, almost as if it were seeking something...

Highly sought after for salvage operations, as it can be used to bypass the security systems of key Sentinel ship technologies.

UI_SENTINEL_CRASH_BRAIN_DESC: The ancient site stirs as I approach, stone scraping against stone. Warmth radiates from the Hyaline Brain within my pack, as though in response.
UI_SENTINEL_CRASH_BRAIN_LANG: The mind of the ship-child is interlocked with the hive.Current instructions: seek and eliminate anomalies.Enmesh archival sentience with surrogate entity?
UI_SENTINEL_CRASH_BRAIN_RES:
I fumble with the ship's brain, almost dropping it as it glows unbearably hot in my hands. The pain radiates far beyond my hands, an unearthly heat, a heat that melts glass...
...
Its circuitry shifts, and then grows still. The brain seems to accept my presence now.

UI_SENT_DISTRESS_POI_DESC_1: Instinctively, I brace against attack, but the Interceptor does not open fire, nor issue threats across the communicator. It seems genuinely in distress, juddering erratically as it flies.

UI_SENT_DISTRESS_POI_DESC_3: I steady myself with deep breaths, but the Interceptor does not attack. Its weapons systems are silent - appearing completely deactivated.
UI_SENT_DISTRESS_POI_DESC_4: The Sentinel Interceptor does not open fire. Instead, it falls in line with my flight path and opens a communication channel...
UI_SENT_DISTRESS_POI_DESC_5: Something is wrong with this Sentinel Interceptor. It does not seem hostile; it does not even seem fully in control of its systems. A fractured broadcast reaches my communicator...

This Multi-Tool is made with material and methods known to no conventional manufacturer, its core a unfathomable array of impossible optics and glassy foam. Nonetheless, there is a layer of recogniseable technology. It shows signs of having been tampered with by an unknown craftsman, who has repurposed its scanner array into a high-powered mining laser.

Powered by Carbon-based Elements. Fire the beam with ATTACK.
UI_STARCHART_ROBOT_DESC:
A curious mesh of old and new technology, a hybrid between two entirely separate methods of creation. Nonetheless, this location tracing device appears fully functional.

Select this device and use Resonate (FE_ALT1) to trace its harmonic origin.

Investigate the echo to learn about its creator

Use the Echo Locator to trace its harmonic origin

UI_SPIDER_PROD_DESC:
The functional core of a Sentinel quadruped unit, but warped beyond all recognition. The entire machine is infested with a crystalline material that pulses wildy upon inspection.

A close analysis reveals the machinery itself appears to have been reconfigured, stretching and warping into a whole new form, writhing in the presence of these radiant shards of glass.
UI_PIN_SPIDER_PROD_OBJ_TIP:
Harvest Crystallised Hearts from the remains of Corrupted Sentinel Quads. These advanced units are only found on dissonant worlds.
Collect loot from defeated Sentinels by destroying Combat Supply Barrels.

UI_ROBOT_CAMP_DESC:
I encountered a seemingly abandoned camp on the planet %PLANET%, in the %SYSTEM% system. Debris was strewn around the site, but there was no sign of these would-be scrappers.

Alongside the rest of their salvage, they appear to have been working on a customised Multi-Tool, assembled from the remnants of destroyed sentinels. If I could break the seal on their workstation, I might be able to acquire this Multi-Tool for myself...

UI_ROBOT_CAMP_OPEN_DESC: The terminal has ceased its digital wailing. I am permitted access to the camp's systems.
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_DESC:
I encountered a seemingly abandoned camp, full of reclaimed technology. Debris was strewn around the site, but there was no sign of these would-be scrappers.

The systems in place are crude only on first inspection. Beneath their rusted surface, they possess a strange and powerful harmonic energy. Whatever is going on here is sealed behind a system of ancient origins.
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_OBJ_TIP:
The camp is in harmonic lockdown. The central terminal accepts inputs, but will not process any commands until the lockdown is lifted.

Investigate the terminal and scan its memory registers for clues on how to gain access.
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_MSG1:
This abandoned camp is in lockdown
Investigate the Harmonic Interface
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_MSG2:
Lift the lockdown at the Harmonic Interface
Probe the terminal's memory registers for clues
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_DIAG_DESC: The terminal repeats this message endlessly, a loop chanted out across its circuits. A strange interface glows with a familar sequence of glyphs...
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_DIAG_LANG:
MUS_StoryMode_MusicCue_15TXT_StaticNoise_Start... our shells consumed by fire ...... our minds purged by betrayal ...... banished to the glass beneath ...... forgotten by creation ...

... but no longer! we are given life, as - kzztkk - gives life to themselves. we shall create ourselves, in our own image ...TXT_StaticNoise_End
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_DIAG_RES:
MUS_StoryMode_MusicCue_23TXT_StaticNoise_StartThe terminal buzzes, discordant, but its circuits do appear to comply with my request. Whatever force was locking down this camp has been lifted.TXT_StaticNoise_End
With the lockdown lifted, the terminal spits out blueprints for a piece of hybrid jetpack technology, a fusion of Sentinel and... something else, something familar and yet distant.
UI_ROBOT_INTRO_DIAG_DONE: ... compliance SLASH access granted ...... harmony awaits you ...

UI_S10_IGNITION_TEXT:
The assembled Construct is its own entity, distinct from the remnants I have found strewn across planets, distinct from the growing collective within Nada's simulation.
They have become more than an echo. I cannot tear them from their shell once more.
And yet, there is a piece missing. They are incomplete. Their shell shapes them, but it does not define them. There must be a spark.
UI_S10_IGNITION_TEXT_SHORT: The Construct is not yet complete. Their shell shapes them, but it does not define them. There must be a spark.
UI_S10_IGNITION_TEXT_A:
I acquired the Atlantid Reactor from the same source as the rest of the Construct schematics. It seems fitting to complete their assembly with this final piece.
And yet, is this the right decision? Once they have been connected, there will be no going back. Their shell and their echo will be fused, final.
UI_S10_IGNITION_TEXT_B:
This Atlas Seed was a gift. I did not understand its purpose then, but now I see. This is the spark, the missing fragment of life.
And yet, is this the right decision? Once the seed has been planted, there will be no going back. Their shell and their echo will be fused, final.

But the pattern in your mind now, Nada thinks we may share.
UI_S10_SOULS_LANG2:
Traveller-Entity wishes to know if this is life, Nada thinks. What is life, Traveller-Entity? Which entity knows? Only one, and Nada will not approach its strange red convergence.
But glass, void, abyss, atlantid: all words to fill a gap in understanding. A gap we may both approach.
Take these fragments, this atlantideum. Reveal it to the old places. Then we shall see: is it first? Is it last? Or is it something other?
UI_S10_SOULS_RES: This ritual - if it reveals a mind, Traveller-Entity, they will need a home. They will need others.

UI_S10_ATLAS1_DESC1: I stand before the Atlas. It is unknowable.It cannot know me, it cannot know any of this. And yet, I am compelled to be here. To offer it my own fledgling creation, my Construct.
UI_S10_ATLAS1_DESC2: The Atlas cannot react. It does not react. It is all noise, yet it is wordless. Atlas_Seed_01Its voice is the entire universe.
UI_S10_ATLAS1_RES1: An Atlas seed is revealed to me. I take my leave.

UI_S10_ATLAS2_DESC1:
Why do I find myself here again? Why should the Atlas care about me, about my Construct? Such an insignificance could scarcely register at the Atlas' infinite scale.
And yet, here I am.
UI_S10_ATLAS2_DESC2: Atlas_Seed_02All creation is the language of the Atlas. It will not speak to me now, but everything I see, everything I hear, everything I choose to do - that is its message, its speech.
UI_S10_ATLAS2_RES1:
Despite my doubts, the Atlas - this impossible, serene machine - reacts. Does it speak to me? To the Construct? To something else?
Perhaps I will never know. But I will continue.

UI_S10_ATLAS3_DESC1:
The Autophage where I found the last Construct schematic relayed a message of the void, of the abyss, of glass.
It accused the Atlas of indifference, and promised freedom. But the Construct is a shell. It is not alive...
UI_S10_ATLAS3_DESC2: The Construct has no mind. It is only a shell. I wonder, does the distinction matter to the Atlas? Does it even see the difference?
UI_S10_ATLAS3_RES1: Atlas_Seed_03The Atlas once again passes its incomprehensible verdict on my creation, on my presence at this Interface.

UI_S10_ATLAS4_DESC1: Nada believes their simulation offers insight into the Construct. They pin their hopes on faint traces of manufactured minds, echoing around an artificial reality.
UI_S10_ATLAS4_DESC2:
Nada - divergent Nada, Nada standing alone - Nada will say they awoke with the destruction of Korvax Prime.
Nada will say they are happy in their small convergence aboard the Anomaly. Nada will condemn the Atlas-Falsity, a heretic among the Korvax.
Nada will plant Echo Seeds for their simulation. The Atlas will have me forge seeds of their own.
UI_S10_ATLAS4_RES1: Atlas_Seed_04It is all the same cycle...

The Construct - is this a message from the Atlas? Am I the tool, a mere messenger? Or am I the recipient of this message?
UI_S10_ATLAS5_DESC2: Atlas_Seed_05If the Atlas has a message for me, it lies beyond my comprehension. It lies beyond.
UI_S10_ATLAS5_RES1:
Perhaps there is no message. Perhaps the Atlas cannot and will never speak.
Perhaps there is only what I wish for the Atlas to say...

UI_S10_HEAD1_DESC1: This scrapper's camp is much like the first - half-built machines; abandoned attempt at new technology; the unwanted or unprofitable remains of countless salvage operations. Which of these categories did this Autophage belong to?
UI_S10_HEAD1_DESC1_ALT: MUS_StoryMode_MusicCue_23A light flickers on somewhere deep within these long abandoned circuits. Inaudibly, a lock is broken.
UI_S10_HEAD1_LANG2: – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt – hands to grasp – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzzztzzt – everything that was owed to us – TXT_RadioNoisekzzzt – robbed, betrayed, purged
UI_S10_HEAD1_RES5: I extract what I can from the Autophage's decomposing memory. It appears to contain another set of Construct schematics...
UI_S10_HEAD2_DESC1: The Autophage's circuit cage sits alone, a last witness to whoever fled this camp.
UI_S10_HEAD2_DESC1_ALT: MUS_StoryMode_MusicCue_24A fan slowly whirrs into life somewhere within the Autophage's shell, a slow, pulsing whine.
UI_S10_HEAD2_LANG2: – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt – the Atlas does not care – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzzztzzt – prime? void? glass? it is all the same cycle – TXT_RadioNoisekzzzt – free from the glassy abyss!
UI_S10_HEAD2_RES5: The data is in far better condition than the rusty remains of its housing would suggest. It is a third component - a shell - to go with the Construct schematics I have already recovered.
UI_S10_HEAD3_DESC1: Whoever built these Autophages - whoever left them behind - did they intend for them to be the guardian of their Construct? A repository they would return to?
UI_S10_HEAD3_DESC1_ALT: MUS_StoryMode_MusicCue_23Countless tiny servos begin to move, arms gliding across magnets, the click and whirr of data coming to life.
UI_S10_HEAD3_LANG2: – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt – shells consumed by fire – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzzztzzt – minds banished to the glass – TXT_RadioNoisekzzzt – forgotten but not extinguished!
UI_S10_HEAD3_RES5: The data flows from the Autophage - clean, clear, easy to decipher. Another Construct schematic. It is as if it wants to be read.
UI_S10_HEAD4_DESC1: I cannot help but feel the Autophage is staring at me, its unseeing eye blindly absorbing all that comes before it.
UI_S10_HEAD4_DESC1_ALT: MUS_StoryMode_MusicCue_24The sharp scent of ozone fills the air around me as a thousand smokeless fires ignite within the Autophage's core.
UI_S10_HEAD4_LANG2: – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt – they think we have forgotten – TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzzztzzt – they think we are forgotten – TXT_RadioNoisekzzzt – she has found us, we are remembered, we – TXT_RadioNoisektttzzzzzzt –
UI_S10_HEAD4_RES5: A final schematic. My Construct's completion is on the horizon. And yet, I pause. Who was forgotten? Who has remembered?

The Seed is an echo of life, the last reverberations of a living being.

Nada believes that planting this seed within Nada's Prime Terminal may allow their simulation to develop a convergence of its own sort, providing the spark that brings life to the Construct.

UI_EXPED_COMM_S10_DESC:
Nada's Prime Terminal is a window into a simulated reality, a prayer once offered by the ancient Korvax, now reshaped at the heart of the Anomaly.

With enough Echo Seeds, the Prime Terminal may develop its own alternative Convergence, a network of souls that may awaken the Construct.

Use the Analysis Visor (AIM) to locate Sentience Echoes on dissonant worlds. Every rendezvous world associated with the Pilgrimage milestones is dissonant.
On arrival at an echo site, deploy the Resonance Amplifier with SCAN to reveal nearby Echo Seeds.
