PC_GRAPHICS_AA_D_V2:
Anti aliasing uses various techniques to smooth out jagged edges around objects (which appear as a result of square pixels forming non-rectangular shapes).

FXAA - Very fast filtering, but can result in a slightly blurred image.

TAA - Fast multi-frame sampling that is sharper than FXAA.

FSR 2.0 - AMD FidelityFX™ Super Resolution 2 is a cutting edge open source temporal upscaling solution, providing high image quality and improved framerates.

Intel XeSS - Intel Xe Super Sampling technology uses machine learning to deliver higher performance with exceptional image quality.

This setting only affects GPU performance.
PC_GRAPHICS_AA_DLSS_D_V2:
Anti aliasing uses various techniques to smooth out jagged edges around objects (which appear as a result of square pixels forming non-rectangular shapes).

FXAA - Very fast filtering, but can result in a slightly blurred image.

TAA - Fast multi-frame sampling that is sharper than FXAA.

FSR 2.0 - AMD FidelityFX™ Super Resolution 2 is a cutting edge open source temporal upscaling solution, providing high image quality and improved framerates.

DLSS - An NVIDIA RTX technology which uses a deep learning neural network to boost frame rates and generate beautiful, sharp images.

DLAA - NVIDIA DLAA is an AI-based anti-aliasing mode for users who have spare GPU headroom and want higher levels of image quality.

Intel XeSS - Intel Xe Super Sampling technology uses machine learning to deliver higher performance with exceptional image quality.

This setting only affects GPU performance.
PC_GRAPHICS_XESS2QUALITY_D:
Intel Xe Super Sampling (XeSS) technology uses machine learning to deliver higher performance with exceptional image quality.

Native - Delivers high quality anti-aliasing and sharpening without any upscaling.

UltraQuality+ - Delivers the highest quality visual upscale (1.3x resolution scaling).

Ultra Quality - Delivers ultra high quality visual upscale (1.3x resolution scaling).

Quality - Delivers high quality visual upscale (1.5x resolution scaling).

Balanced - Delivers optimal performance and image quality (1.7x resolution scaling).

Performance - Improves overall gaming performance (2.0x resolution scaling).

Ultra Performance - Offers the highest performance boost (3.0x resolution scaling). Recommended for 8K resolutions only.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%

This setting only affects GPU performance.
PC_GRAPHICS_DLSSFRAMEGEN_D_V2:
Frame Generation boosts frame rates by using AI to render additional frames.

Off - Turns DLSS Frame Generation off.

2X - The total number of frames is doubled, with one rendered and one generated frame. Supported on a GeForce RTX 40 Series graphics card or higher.

3X - The total number of frames is tripled, with one rendered and two generated frames. Supported on a GeForce RTX 50 Series graphics card.

4X - The total number of frames is quadrupled, with one rendered and three generated frames. Supported on a GeForce RTX 50 Series graphics card.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_OPTION_SUIT_VOICE_D:
Sets the vocal style for situations reported verbally by the Exosuit Artificial Intelligence (such as when receiving Units).

Feminine Suit Voice - The Exosuit speaks with a feminine voice. Available in all languages.

Masculine Suit Voice - The Exosuit speaks with a masculine voice. Available in English only.

Suit Voice Off - The Exosuit does not speak.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%
UI_OPTION_PLAYER_VOICE_D:
Sets the vocal range for vocalisations (such as breathing and grunts) made by the player character.

Player Voice A - The player character vocalises in a higher pitch.

Player Voice B - The player character vocalises in a lower pitch.

Player Voice C - The player character vocalises in more exotic, alien tones.

Vocalisations Off - The player character does not vocalise.

Default value is: %DEFAULTVALUE%

UI_STA_DECOR_DESC: A free-floating adornment, to add decorative character to orbital constructions.
UI_STA_STRUCT_DESC: A free-floating Space Station extension, to add decorative character to orbital constructions.
UI_STA_POI_DESC: A rare orbital construction adornment, recovered from deep space.
BLD_STA_CORR_DESC:
This pressurised corridor intelligently adjoins to existing rooms, connecting habitable spaces in orbital constructions.

This flexible corridor piece will automatically expand and contract to form curves or junctions when placed.
BLD_STA_CORR_STAIRS_DESC: A sturdy, non-slip staircase with an ergonomic incline, for traversing vertically between storeys.
BLD_STA_CORR_A_GLASS_DESC:
This pressurised corridor intelligently adjoins to existing rooms, connecting habitable spaces in orbital constructions. The low-expansion, radiation-proof glass ceiling allows a view into deep space.

This flexible piece will automatically expand and contract to form curves or junctions when placed.
BLD_STA_CORR_STAIRS_G_DESC:
A sturdy, non-slip staircase with an ergonomic incline, for traversing vertically between storeys.

Constructed from low thermal expansion glass, these stairs provide the user with a thrilling view into deep space.
BLD_FRE_ROOM_B_DESC: A spacious chamber with a commercial aesthetic, for expanding habitable spaces inside large spaceships.
BLD_STA_ROOM_B_DESC: A spacious chamber with a commercial aesthetic, for expanding habitable spaces in orbital constructions.
BLD_STA_FACE_WALL_DESC: An interior wall to subdivide large habitable spaces. Seamlessly configures itself to fit the aesthetics of the surrounding room.
BLD_STA_FACE_WINDOW_DESC:
A pane of low thermal expansion glass.

Can be fitted into orbital constructions to open up a view into space.
BLD_STA_FACE_DOOR_DESC:
A thick, robust door.

Hermetically sealed for installation in orbital constructions, or between internal corridors and rooms.
BLD_STA_EXT_WALKWAY_DESC:
This exterior walkway intelligently adjoins to existing rooms, creating decking outside orbital constructions.

A Reinforced Door must be installed to allow access to exterior spaces.
BLD_STA_CORR_STAIRS_EXT_DESC:
A sturdy, non-slip staircase with an ergonomic incline, for traversing vertically between storeys.

These robust stairs can be affixed outside an orbital construction, creating connections between exterior catwalks and platforms.
BLD_STA_EXT_DESC:
An unsheltered observation deck. Allows the user to step outside an orbital construction, and gaze directly into the vastness of space.

A Reinforced Door must be installed to allow access to exterior spaces.
BLD_STA_ROOM_LADDER_DESC:
An inbuilt ladder for traversing vertically between storeys.

Attaches directly to corridors.
BLD_STA_ROOM_TELEPO_DESC:
This personal teleport device allows the user to move quickly between their freighter, bases, as well as any Space Station Terminuses connected to their network. User is urged to verify network integrity before inserting any matter they cannot afford to become separated from.

This module is placed as an entire room and comes with its functional units pre-installed.
BLD_STA_ROOM_DRESS_DESC:
Integrated equipment allowing the user to adjust their personal appearance settings. This module is placed as an entire room and comes with its functional units pre-installed.

The module applies advanced holographic techniques to recalibrate the light around the user, allowing them to adopt whatever appearance they desire. Visual data must be properly formatted before use.
BLD_STA_ROOM_SHOP_DESC:
Integrated equipment providing instant local access to the galactic trade market for resources and commodities.

This module is placed as an entire room and comes with its functional units pre-installed.
BLD_STA_ROOM_TECH_DESC: A spacious chamber with a technical aesthetic, for expanding habitable spaces inside orbital constructions.
BLD_STA_ROOM_REFINER_DESC:
The Refiner Room allows three different substances to be processed into more powerful and more advanced materials.

This module is placed as an entire room and comes with its functional units pre-installed.
BLD_STA_ROOM_EXTR_DESC:
Gathers resources directly from the interstellar medium, via a complex system of suction intakes and condensing tubes. The gathered substance varies with the local star classification.

This module is placed as an entire room and comes with its functional units pre-installed.
BLD_STA_ROOM_IND_DESC: A spacious chamber with an industrial aesthetic, for expanding habitable spaces inside orbital constructions.
BLD_STA_ROOM_STORE_DESC:
Hybrid high-capacity storage unit / shelving module for installation in orbital constructions. This module is placed as an entire room and comes with its functional units pre-installed.

Inventory capacity interfaces directly with planetary Storage Containers, and the module may be renamed for ease of identification.
UI_SPACE_BASE_DESC:
Orbital volume registration service.

When placed, contacts Universal Cartographic Archive to establish ownership of a volume in deep space. Successful registration allows the construction of base modules across any site of the user's choosing.
UI_SPACE_BASE_ANYWHERE_NEW:
Searching cartographic archives...
Universal Archive Search reveals no prior claims in this volume. Anomaly scan confirms the volume is suitable for construction. Claim volume?
UI_SPACE_BASE_ANYWHERE_SUCCESS:
Base registered to current owner. Upload and construction permissions granted. Note: uploading will overwrite any previous uploaded space bases for this system.
Use the Space Station Terminus to teleport to the base at any time.

Station directors have the right to modify key structures, including external decoration, interior layout and ancillary compartments.

The director may also found a galactic alliance, or ally their station with an existing alliance.

Note: regulations require that core services and functions provided by the station must be preserved for all visitors.

UI_SO_COLLECT_H_DESC_1: Local communications are awash with reports of wreckage adrift in the system. No one has laid claim to the wreck yet, as such it should be ripe for the picking.
UI_SO_COLLECT_H_DESC_2: The client has identified the location of a wrecked freighter. They require the recovery of specific items from the wreckage. Locate the wreckage and extract these items for the client.
UI_SO_COLLECT_H_DESC_3: A local starship dealer requires second-hand parts to replenish their stock of spares. Recover the items for the dealer and remember, expense can be spared.
UI_SO_COLLECT_H_DESC_4: This contract grants full salvage rights of any wrecks found in this system to the contract holder, with the exception of the items requested by the contract. Failure to return said items to the contract issuer will void these salvage rights.
UI_SO_COLLECT_H_DESC_5: The client has been researching the disappearance of a Merchants Guild vessel whose course passed through this region of space. Their investigation has led them to a cluster of stars around this star system. They are seeking a local, experienced salvaging operation to locate the wreck and return with evidence of the wreck being found.

Customise your station with a wide range of decorative parts and build a modular interior annexe that other visitors to the station can access. Blueprints for parts can be purchased at the Construction Research Terminal on board the Space Anomaly.

UI_S23_LEAVE_PLANET_LOG:
No Man's Sky was an idea that maybe everyone who plays games has thought about at some point. What if you could explore the universe? What if a game world didn't have boundaries? It's certainly something we had always wanted to see exist...

For us there was a technical excitement. No one had done seamless travel between planets, or used procedural generation to make 3D planets - but it should be possible? And wouldn't it be fun to try?

There was also an emotional motivation. We wanted to really have that feeling of exploration in a game, true exploration where no one knows what's over the hill. That science fiction fantasy of landing on a planet for the first time.

So sat in our little office one night, we started to build it. There was never really a plan, we had no idea how wild a journey it would become, but it felt exciting.
UI_S23_BUILD_BASE_LOG:
Foundation was really the beginning of our journey. We had the idea to name our updates, and to give each one a sci-fi book cover. We always loved Asimov, and Foundation as a name felt like a fitting tribute, because this was going to also be a starting point we would build on.

We liked the idea of letting players put down roots in an infinite universe, it wasn't really what players were asking for, but it has become fundamental to No Man's Sky as we know it now.

We also introduced game modes for the first time: Normal, Creative, and Survival. With these changes Foundation pointed to our future, allowing players to find their own way to experience the universe.

The whole thing was created in just three months under a lot of pressure, with just a handful of developers. This update was made in our old tiny office down near the River Wey in Guildford. We had no air con, a venomous spider who lived in the toilets, and failing internet.

UI_S23_BUILD_EXO_ANY_LOG:
The planets in No Man's Sky are vast, but players tended to jump in their ship even for short-distance journeys. We wanted to find a way to make planetary traversal fun, and fast. Several of the team had worked on racing games like Burnout or Need for Speed at EA, and we had a lot of experience with vehicles from our first game Joe Danger! So it was really exciting to introduce sci-fi themed vehicles to the No Man's Sky universe.

In Pathfinder, we added buggies, hovercrafts, and a heavy-duty armoured truck. We deepened a number of existing systems too, introducing base uploads and new weapon types, and a Permadeath mode for extreme challenge seekers. Making our generation keep up with these new vehicle speeds was a particularly difficult but fun challenge.
UI_S23_WAKE_TITAN_LOG:
By 2017 we knew there was a core community of players who loved the game, and they were the people we deeply cared about. We desperately wanted to find a way to communicate with them and let them know we were listening, whilst we focused on the game.

Then the thought came: we've always loved ARGs! What about an Augmented Reality Game? This became Waking Titan.

We posted physical cassette tapes to 16 prominent members of the NMS community, and invited players to explore a website filled with cyphers and mysterious documents. Players travelled to real world live drop locations, and met with agents from the mysterious "Atlas Foundation". There was a live stream of a hamster. We loved it!

Together with the ARG puppet masters, it felt like we were enjoying a game with friends in the community. Some of our ideas went a bit too far. We were advised that our insurance didn't cover inviting players into the studio and arming them with blowtorches to extract a key from an ice sculpture. We still think that would have been fine.

UI_S23_ARTEMIS_LOG:
At launch, the guided story was very light touch. Most of the game's lore was fragmented, discovered through exploration, and there were only a couple of recurring non-player characters.

For Atlas Rises, we crafted a massive 30-hour story, introducing new characters and a new interdimensional race. As a first step toward true multiplayer, we allowed players to see each other as floating orbs, and tied this into the evolution of the game's lore.

Our aim with updates became to always deepen and expand existing features while also adding new ones. Atlas Rises brought wealth and conflict levels to the galactic economy, as well as adding exotic biomes and the exotic ship class.

Development on this update was a whirlwind, we added so much in such a short space of time. We had to code a brand-new mission system to support the story, and the ending wasn't implemented until the night before launch! (We have learned to be a little better planned now. Most of the time.)

UI_S23_NEXT_LOG:
NEXT came at the conclusion of phase two of Waking Titan. This was a huge milestone for No Man's Sky. We always knew we wanted to add full multiplayer, but once we started making and animating third-person models, it just made sense to add a third-person mode too. We hadn't anticipated how much it would help highlight the scale of the universe - seeing a person-sized figure next to a huge structure literally helps put it into perspective.

We launched a website showcasing the community, and started weekly community events. We added new enemies, planetary rings, volumetric clouds, frigate fleets, and the ability to build multiple bases, anywhere, without needing to locate a pre-placed base computer. We also reworked the terrain generation algorithm to improve the shape of planets - something players often ask for, but which comes at the cost of disrupting existing bases. There are still bases out there that were buried when the terrain moved.

Releasing NEXT was nerve-wracking, but the community response was incredible, a real turning point. Our global user rating even progressed from Mostly Negative to Mixed! We mixed now bois!

UI_S23_EXO_BIKE_LOG:
After NEXT, we wanted to try a more regular rhythm of smaller releases before the next huge named update.

We surveyed the community to get a sense of what players wanted most, and planned out an "underwater update", which became The Abyss, a "biomes update", which became Visions, and an "exocraft update"...

...which introduced the Pilgrim exocraft, exocraft customisation, techs, and other improvements... and which we quietly blogged about under the unassuming title Development Update 5.

At this point we were still trying to figure out whether to do yearly huge updates or more regular, smaller ones.

UI_S23_BEYOND_LOG:
Beyond was a massive update, and development was intense. We had two parts of the team working in parallel on two huge, technically challenging new features: virtual reality support, and expanded multiplayer.

Up until now, the full multiplayer experience with third-person character models was limited to 4 people per session, and there was no way to ambiently meet strangers in-game. With Beyond we expanded the Space Anomaly into a social hub, where it was easy to meet and group up with other players. We added stacks of new content too - including multiplayer missions, new NPCs, base power, tech trees, and cooking.

One thing we didn't anticipate was how different the world looked when playing VR. You have no idea what its like to work on this game for ten years, then see it with fresh eyes! One knock on was having to dramatically increase the size of all the ships in the game to make them look their best in VR - which also made landing pads bigger across the game, which in turn impacted the size and position of buildings and space stations!

UI_S23_BYTEBEAT_LOG:
Synthesis was an effort to consolidate, tidy and polish the game across the board, in response to the most frequent requests from the community. Addressing player feedback isn't always straightforward, and some solutions might not always lead to the best result, so we designed Synthesis' features with a lot of thought and care. Remembering back it's funny to think there was a time before you could drag and drop items in the inventory, when you could only own one Multi-Tool, and when you couldn't undo terrain manipulations.

Two weeks later we released something very different: the Bytebeat audio synthesiser for bases. This was a passion project dreamed up by one of our coders and our audio director. We always knew it would be a niche feature, but even now the creative players who engage with it continue to regularly bring us joy, 7 years later.

UI_S23_WEEKEND_LOG:
With NEXT, we introduced community missions, which were a sort of precursor to today's community expeditions. We had the idea that we wanted to bring large groups of players together on the same planet, working towards the same goal, and that collaborative progress would unlock special rewards for the whole community.

The name of the special new reward currency, Quicksilver, was a suggestion from our ARG partners from Waking Titan. Quicksilver is an archaic word for mercury, which has the atomic symbol Hg. "The mercury process" was the name we gave to messages from HG - Hello Games - during the ARG.

In late 2019, we started running community missions regularly on weekends. They began with some light narrative that eventually evolved into a deep mystery involving the inhabitants of the Space Anomaly. We've never completely revealed all the secrets of that storyline. Special missions are still available every weekend, and are now procedurally generated rather than hand-authored.

UI_S23_BUILD_MECH_LOG:
Exo Mech was another artist-led update. One of our artists just really wanted to make a mech! The aesthetic appealed to the rest of the team, and it seemed like a good fit for a new style of exocraft. It all came together really quickly.

In the middle of development on Exo Mech, the UK government started releasing information and warnings about the outbreak of a new coronavirus. At the start of March, a few volunteers from the team "trialled" working from home. Within a fortnight the entire team was fully remote. It was a weird transition for a small team who were used to working very closely together in the same space, but we made it work. Somehow we stayed just as productive as before, and a very busy year of updates followed. We kept socially connected with regular evening games of Among Us, and a weekly film club that kept going for 70 weeks.

UI_S23_DO_ABAND_F_LOG:
Desolation might be the darkest update we've made for No Man's Sky, leaning into the space horror side of sci fi. Perhaps we were feeling the effects of being locked down after all! It took a bit of iteration to get the rules for the procedural generation of these huge space hulks feeling correct. Making the spaces interesting to explore without being frustrating to navigate without a mini-map is a fun problem. All the generation happens behind the scenes, in the moment you unlock the airlock door.

Just after Desolation, we added cross-play support, to let Travellers across all platforms play together, and added a custom system for adding players from other platforms as "No Man's Sky friends". Not many other games were doing this at the time and it was a huge undertaking.

No Man's Sky is generated using maths, and each platform has different hardware that results in tiny differences in how their maths are calculated. For instance some maths differences between platforms meant the space stations had always been generated in slightly different positions before this update!

UI_S23_ORIGINS_LOG:
No Man's Sky has always been a game about exploration and discovery, and players were often asking us to give them more variety on planets, more places to explore. But the difficulty is balancing that against players who are attached to existing planets. It broke our heart in the past when we changed generation and had people write in to say that they've named a planet or built a base in memory of a family member, and now that planet has a different climate or terrain shape or grass colour.

So in Origins we took a two-pronged approach to refreshing the universe: we "remixed" existing biomes, vastly increasing the variety of landscapes players could encounter, and we added brand new planets so we could create dramatic new terrain shapes without disrupting anyone's bases. With new creature types, new buildings, and a huge injection of variety it really felt like stepping into a new universe for the first time. We also introduced huge sandworms, roaming the landscape, which have gone on to create some of our favorite moments with streamers and players over the years.
UI_S23_GOT_PETS_LOG:
The procedurally-generated creatures in No Man's Sky are an ongoing source of joy. They still make us laugh. The team still sends screenshots and videos around when we find a particularly beautiful, surprising or funny animal. We wanted to add more ways for players to interact with them, to make them feel more connected and alive.

The design for Companions went through several iterations. At one point, the concept revolved around collecting DNA samples from wild creatures to grow new life in a laboratory setting, but in playtesting we found it was more satisfying to hunt down and adopt a pet, similar to hunting down the perfect ship. We love seeing players sharing images of their weird and wonderful pets.
UI_S23_PIONEERS_LOG:
The average playtime is really high on No Man's Sky, and that's something we're proud of. Sometimes players send us saves that are 2000 or 3000 hours long! But there's something special about starting from the beginning, starting from nothing, with a crashed ship on an unfamiliar planet - that's the best bit of any sandbox game - and we wanted to find a way to give that moment back to players. 

The Expeditions system was a natural evolution of the community missions and weekend missions we'd been running for a few years - bringing players together - and it also encouraged seasoned players to re-experience those first steps stranded on a strange planet.

The first expedition we launched was called "Pioneers". Subsequent expeditions have become more experimental and weird as time has gone by... We've been surprised and delighted with how popular they are amongst players, and have gone on to create some incredible moments we couldn't have predicted.

UI_S23_PRISMS_LOG:
The backbone of No Man's Sky is our custom engine, which we continue to expand and improve with every update.

As well as handling the memory and performance challenges that come with an infinite, procedurally-generated universe running on two generations of consoles, our engine team are constantly pushing graphical limits to make that universe just a little more beautiful. 

Some of our rendering improvements come from art team requests, and others are driven from within the engine team itself. In Prisms, we tried to gather and showcase a bunch of graphical improvements all at once: adding things like volumetric lighting, screen-space reflections, and furry creatures. We work on No Man's Sky every day motivated by the technical endeavour as much as that sci-fi fantasy.

UI_S23_FRONTIERS_LOG:
We started experimenting with an algorithm called wave function collapse, in combination with our base building system, to procedurally generate complex buildings. The design went through several iterations before we landed on exactly what we wanted to do with the technology. We started making abandoned bases for players to clean out and restore, but in the end what appealed was creating Mos Eisley-feeling settlements populated by aliens. 

This became Frontiers. Creating and rendering these settlements was a huge undertaking, the culmination of years of work and really pushed what was possible with our engine. It opened up a lot of possibilities for the future.

After years of positive reviews, our rating progressed from "Mixed" to "Mostly Positive". A huge milestone for the team, we made "Mostly Positive" t-shirts for everyone, which is basically just a good message on a tee.

UI_S23_MINIWORMS_LOG: Expeditions are a great way for us to try out new ideas that we think players would enjoy, but wouldn't necessarily fit with the core game. Almost little experiments or alternative realities. In some ways, Emergence is a love letter to the likes of Dune, but we had a lot of fun making our own body-horror themed lore for this. There is a creepy side to sci-fi that is so fun to explore.
UI_S23_RAID_HIVE_LOG:
No Man's Sky is a game about exploration and combat may not be the main focus, but Sentinels patrol almost every planet. We wanted to make fighting them feel more tactical and interesting.

The Sentinel update added different varieties of Sentinel drones - repair drones, heavies, and summoners. We improved the feel of ground combat across the board with lots of new abilities and tech. We even created a new story-based mission for players to construct their own drone companion, and upgrade their Exo-Mech! This was supposed to be a smaller update but in the end the patch notes amounted to more than 250 items!
UI_S23_OUTLAWS_LOG:
Our updates often come together like this. One person had made a ship with holographic sails - the Solar ship. A programmer had gotten cloth physics working, perhaps now we could have flowing capes? Another artist was making a cool underworld themed space station... 

We were aware that some players really liked to engage with the space piracy fantasy. Capes? Sail ships? Underground space station? What if we made a pirate focused update? And so Outlaws was born!

This idea unlocked so much creativity in the team, with tons of new content and gameplay.
UI_S23_LEVIATHAN_LOG:
Many of our community expeditions ran alongside named updates - Cartographers, Exobiology and The Blight were concurrent with Frontiers, Sentinel, and Outlaws. The Leviathan expedition became so visually striking, and the gameplay was so unique that we felt it needed its own trailer, and we released it standalone. 

The idea came together from the artists wanting to make a biological frigate, and the designers wanting to craft an expedition around roguelike gameplay. It was our most different, but also our most popular expedition - exciting us to go further with expeditions in the future.

UI_S23_ENDURANCE_LOG:
Endurance hugely changed the scope of building a base on your freighter, a feature which had been largely untouched since introduced in Foundation. It was especially exciting to be able to build exterior catwalks and observation decks - something not possible before... 

Rendering windows and exterior walkways in space is a particularly hard technical problem. The moment we first saw the view from the deck, we just knew we had to support it.

In fact the way we built freighters initially used a lot of smoke and mirrors and this made it particularly hard to support most of these new features. For instance, newer players might not remember a time before you could teleport from the freighter hangar to the bridge... such a great quality of life improvement! Even just that simple feature required some real technical wizardry going on behind the scenes to make that work.
UI_S23_WAYPOINT_LOG:
By 2022, No Man's Sky had been evolving for six years, and we had added a lot of new content and new layers. It was always important to us to keep the game accessible to new players. We wanted folks to be able to jump in and be excited by the possibilities of the universe, but not feel overwhelmed. Waypoint was a concentrated effort to more clearly surface information about the universe as you discovered it. We cleaned up the in-game catalogue, and added journal-style records of progress through the core narrative.

We also completely unpicked the concept of game modes, which had remained the same since the introduction of Permadeath back in Pathfinder. We tried to allow players to play exactly as they wanted, letting them focus on whatever their favourite area of the game was - basebuilding, exploration, resource acquisition, story, combat, survival - the game means a lot of different things to a lot of different people.
UI_S23_WAYPOINT_LOG_EXTRA_NX: This is also when we launched on Nintendo Switch! We honestly weren't sure whether it was possible at first, but our crazy engine team tend to interpret the word "impossible" as "thrilling technical challenge"!

UI_S23_FRACTAL_LOG: Fractal was an opportunity for the team to give No Man's Sky another scrub and coat of polish. We improved graphics, increased accessibility, and launched the Utopia expedition. We also added "Wonders" to showcase the most remarkable discoveries among the thousands players would amass on their journeys. This was something we'd wanted for a long time.
UI_S23_FRACTAL_LOG_EXTRA_PS:
The heart of Fractal was really the release of PSVR2, and the VR enthusiasts in the team went to town improving every aspect of the experience in virtual reality, from gameplay to performance and rendering. We added flat-screen support for left-handed mode, and some players speculated that this was a prelude to left-handed support in VR. They were right! 

In games development often the things that sound hard are easy, and the easy sounding things are hard! The saying is "everything is smoke and mirrors, apart from smoke and mirrors which we have to do a different way". Left handed mode was a passion project, but a silly amount of special case work in VR for one hero on the team who really cared.
UI_S23_INTERCEPTOR_LOG:
What if you could commandeer and fly a Sentinel ship?

Interceptor started with that idea, allowing players to take something back from the relentless system authorities (who we affectionately refer to as "the space police" internally). It soon grew into something much bigger. The designers and artists dreamt up the concept of dissonant planets, with mysterious robot heads, apparently empty campsites, and Sentinel forces corrupted by an otherworldly purple crystal. This update came together especially quickly - everything just flowed and fell into place. It's an amazing feeling when that happens.

No Man's Sky now had more than seven platform variants. It was a lot, especially for a small team, and we weren't done yet...
UI_S23_ECHOES_LOG:
Interceptor, the Singularity expedition (where players helped Specialist Polo construct a robot) and now finally the Echoes update were all designed as a sort of breadcrumb trail to introduce a new alien race we had been working on: the robotic Autophage. 

Narratively, these Korvax-derived lifeforms have always inhabited the universe, so we came up with a "scan to reveal" mechanic to unveil them to Travellers. We also introduced the "modular customisation" system in Echoes, allowing players to construct their own staff Multi-Tool. That system proved to be very versatile. The same underlying code enabled modular ship construction in Orbital, and fossil assembly in Relics.

Echoes also brought in Dreadnought freighter battles, with a trench run gameplay loop inspired by a favourite scene in one of our favourite sci-fi franchises. We love that No Man's Sky can support this action side of sci-fi as well as more reflective exploration.

UI_S23_ORBITAL_LOG:
Orbital, Omega and the Adrift expedition all released in fairly quick succession in early 2024! 

Omega was an especially challenging update. We essentially built a demo in the form of a free expedition, which has different technical requirements on different platforms, and which also had to serve as a sort of tutorial for new players. We also allowed players to start expeditions from existing saves - something the community had been requesting for a while - which required some delicate data-masking and context-handling of save games. We always feel extremely cautious around anything related to save data. Many of our players have thousands of hours of progress by now.

Orbital introduced two massive features we'd been working on for a while: a complete redesign of space stations, and constructable starships.

Some players have been wanting to customise ships forever, but ship-hunting is such a core part of No Man's Sky that we couldn't simply remove that feature. Instead, we implemented the ability to collect modules and construct new ships from scratch, while acknowledging naturally-occurring ships with an "authenticated" badge.

We decided not to redesign the abandoned versions of space stations. It feels somehow fitting that they are a relic of the old design...

UI_S23_WORLDS1_LOG:
Worlds Part I and Part II were originally conceived as one big update. We wanted to refresh exploration by completely overhauling the visuals and diversity of the universe. 

As often happens with our updates, but with this one in particular... it got huge. Everyone on the team had more and more ideas, and more features they wanted to cram in. We decided to split the update in half, and get features to players sooner. Part I focused on improving existing planets, saving adding entirely new planets for Part II. 

Years of work came together to allow us to transform water from a fixed sphere to a dynamic, responsive mesh. Meanwhile we rewrote the cloud generation system from scratch. Finally the person who constantly replied to every social media post with "fix clouds" could rest.
UI_S23_CATCH_RARE_FISH_LOG:
We work very quickly at Hello, with more of a game jam kind of vibe. New team members who join us from other studios often comment how fast new features come together. Fishing was one of those features! We saw a fan posting about how cool fishing would be, and just weeks later our fishing update was releasing! We designed the Aquarius expedition around it and we love that it's a very chill way for people to spend time together on a planet. Seeing screenshots of lots of players fishing side-by-side makes us so happy.

For Halloween, we put together a spooky expedition called The Cursed, which started with the idea of limiting interstellar travel to the portal network, and grew to introduce elements like spectral squids and a sped-up day/night cycle.

In November 2024, our global user rating progressed from "Mostly Positive" to "Very Positive". We got some "Very Positive" socks made for the team, which you only wear when you are really feeling it.
UI_S23_WORLDS2_LOG:
When we split Worlds into two updates, we had intended to release Worlds Part II shortly afterwards. The player response to Part I was so positive that we thought actually, we want to listen to feedback and spend longer perfecting Part II. Of course, that meant it grew even bigger!

We added a bunch of new biomes and creatures, as well as even more improvements to water rendering. We made "abandoned mode", an idea first introduced in Adrift, into a complete game mode. Perhaps most significantly, we added entirely new star systems - something we hadn't done since launch - which gave the narrative team a really exciting opportunity for building a new story. It gave us the freedom to add new terrain shapes and waterworlds. Finally we could add gas giants, something we had dreamt of since launch.

In the background we are also working on an ambitious new game, Light No Fire. Some key tech developed for this was now being sent back - almost from the future - for No Man's Sky, allowing us to keep expanding the universe.
UI_S23_GOT_FOSSILS_LOG:
The idea for Relics came from one of our team playing Animal Crossing with their daughter. The idea of collecting fossils for a bone museum fit perfectly with several elements of No Man's Sky: exploration, collecting, procedurally generated creatures, and the modular customisation system we'd established back in Echoes.

Video game publications cover No Man's Sky pretty regularly, but this update earnt us a tongue-in-cheek article in a museum industry magazine. The author noted that "While Relics is certainly fun, as a museum professional there is a lot that I found concerning." "I'm [...] troubled that said relics are then promptly shipped off to your home planet to be displayed in your own private (unaccredited) museum."

The idea of collecting fossils for a bone museum fit perfectly with several elements of No Man's Sky: exploration, collecting, procedurally generated creatures, and the modular customisation system we'd established back in Echoes.

UI_S23_BEACON_LOG:
We'd had an internal wishlist of improvements for Settlements for a while, and we were excited by the idea of adding settlements for the new Autophage lifeforms. Beacon combined those two design objectives into an update that the community wasn't expecting at all. It's always our aim to be surprising!

Some of the proposed names for this update included "Betterments", "Frontierier", "Robotopolis", and "Do Androids Dream Of Big Purple Settlements". Thankfully, none of those were taken seriously.

UI_S23_BIGGS_BUILD_LOG:
Voyagers was one of our most challenging updates to develop. Having multi-crew star ships you could walk around in, in multiplayer, while travelling at light speed is a very hard problem. Retrofitting it to an existing game is even harder. From when it was first working though, you could just tell how incredible it would feel.

Effectively we were using the base building system to create the ships, then flying those ships through space with networked players inside, sometimes on different gaming platforms, warping between systems together. We had some fantastic bugs in the weeks before launch. Planetary base parts were taking off and flying into space! Our IK system was warping players legs between ships like a scene from a Cronenberg film. Players would warp their ship full of friends to new systems, and accidentally scatter them stranded throughout space.

The team worked incredibly hard to solve all these issues, and more - and the reception when we released was genuinely unexpected. We saw the highest number of players since launch! We couldn't believe some of the wild creativity we were seeing from players. Meticulous reproductions of favourite classic sci-fi ships, but also using unusual base parts to create flying forests and galleons and ships with eyes and limbs. It made all that challenge worth it!
UI_S23_REMNANT_LOG:
After the physics tech we'd developed for Voyagers, we were hungry to add more physical elements to the gameplay of No Man's Sky. Remnant was originally conceived with the plan to use multiple physics worlds for loading cargo into your exocraft - the same technology that allows players to stand inside a Corvette and not get jettisoned into space when it moves. 

We tried that... it was ok... but we struck upon something much more fun. Introducing a gravity gun we embraced the chaos of physics and allowed the cargo to jiggle and bounce with the movement of the Colossus - and sometimes have precious cargo fall out. As we saw at launch, there were some great moments during development of precious cargo rolling down hill at the last moment.
UI_S23_PET_BATTLES_LOG:
One of our team had a passion for turn-based multiplayer games, and a bunch of experience with developing them. We could see how turn-based games would fit with our multiplayer model, and so the concept of "game tables" was born. We loved the idea of having a game for players to play in more chill moments together.

Xeno Arena came from that love of pet battler games, and the creatures in No Man's Sky. We had always wanted to make more of the pets you collect in No Man's Sky, maybe we could combine the two? 

At the start of development, we were hand-crafting every possible battle move, but it quickly became clear that we would need a vast number of moves to make battles fun to play repeatedly - far more than our tiny team could author by hand. So we built a procedural generation system to assign unique moves to each creature, and the result is hundreds of abilities, and a mini-game with a surprising amount of depth.

UI_S23_FUTURE_LOG:
Our most recent update is Cosmos, bringing together a number of highly-requested features, and some we dreamt up internally: space station ownership, shipbreaking, and lots of points of interest in space! 

All this time we have been a space game, and yet space felt like it could be much more alive. It's wild to us that ten years in, there are still so many unexplored areas of development like this, and they are still so exciting to us. We feel lucky to have that opportunity.

We love making this game. It means so much to us that most of the people in that "gold master disc" photo from a decade ago are still at Hello Games. It means so much that so many of you, our players, have been on this journey with us since day one - and that newer Travellers are joining us all the time.

Thank you. So much.

Our journey continues.

NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO_LANG: Traveller-Friend! Are you safe? We are reading large dark signals, Nada and I. It is familiar signal, but - well - are you safe?
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO_A_LANG:
You do not remember Polo?
Oh, friend. You are more fragmented than I knew.
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO_B_DESC: I describe my brief encounter with Hive of Glass, and the swarm of ships it left behind to pursue me.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO_B_LANG2: Please, friend, do not be like that! Do not be so brave! This thing, it cannot be safe...
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO_B_DESC2: Polo shakes their head, though the hint of a smile plays at the corner of their beak.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO_B_LANG3: And these small swarms. You say they released an essence, a substance? Something physical. This I would like to learn more from.
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO_C_DESC: I try to describe the vision I had before waking, though I find the details slipping from my memory. A sense of being questioned, assessed. Something about a %TEAMNAME% fragment. Polo squints at me through the communicator.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO_C_LANG: I know. I can see. You are fragmented, all - TXT_RadioNoisekzzt - of you...
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO_D_DESC: I explain about the apparition in my ship, and how I reforged their data into a new pilot signature.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO_D_LANG:
Your ship did not see you as you?
This Echo-Friend - they are not where or when they should be. But I am happy they wanted to help. Traveller has always been kind.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO_END: I think it is time for you to be here. Come to the Anomaly, friend. Our home is a place of safety.
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO1_DESC: Polo looks at me, their expression thoughtful. Whatever is on their mind, they do not voice it.
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO2_DESC: They pause, staring at the ichor in their hands. When they speak, it is not to me.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO2_LANG2: It may explain the signals. A match, but only partial.
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO2_DESC2: The Gek takes a deep breath. They smile broadly, as though to reassure me.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO2_LANG3: Thank you, friend! I will take some time with this. It is in my mind now. Cast it from yours!
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO2_A_LANG:
Yes. We have seen the swarm evidence too. Shadows across the loom!
These swarmers are many. Expendable. One, Nada and I traced to the very end of its signal. Its crash site may give more answers!
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO2_B_LANG: I can see it more clearly with you - TXT_RadioNoisekzzt - here. You are you, but only a fragment. The %TEAMNAME% - TXT_RadioNoisekzzt - I do not - TXT_RadioNoisekzzt -
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO2_B_DESC: Polo winces. They fall silent, apparently closing the subject for now.
NPC_S22_REPORT1_POLO3_LANG: I was sure you would ask, friend. It is done! Your research may deepen our understanding.
UI_S22_REPORT1_POLO3_DESC: Polo transmits the approximate location of the swarmer crash site to my starship computer.

- TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt - you must - TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt - return - TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt - the hive - TXT_RadioNoisekzkzzt -
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO_LANG: The Hive - it is still here, yes? Signal is not gone. Patterns are still dark.
UI_S22_REPORT2_POLO2_DESC: I try to explain what happened during the confrontation with the Hive. Polo's features wrinkle with anxiety.
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO2_LANG: This story scares me, Traveller-Friend. None of this is right. This Hive is not where it should be. You are not all of you.
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO2_LANG2: Nada and I, we have been trying to forecast. It is not enough to wait and worry! I have started to build.
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO3_LANG: You saw prismatic core, yes? By the entrance to our home. It is mirror of where the swarm is swarming. And more, I hope!
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO4_LANG: I am tracking data with core. I have theory. A plan!
UI_S22_REPORT2_POLO4_DESC: Polo's tone shifts, the enthusiasm of planning overtaking their worry.
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO4_LANG2:
Hive is familiar. It seems like Atlas, but not quite Atlas. It fixates on you. All of you.
Hive is not Crimson Hunter, no, but part of. Just in wrong place.
Core is more than mirror. It is combination engine. If all fragments recombine, reflect back at swarm, we can also reflect back at Hive. Reflect things back to right place!
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO4_LANG3: Bigger data will build bigger core. Tidy reality of things that should not be here. It is a good plan, yes?
NPC_S22_REPORT2_POLO4_RES: Take closer look at core, friend! You will see plan!

UI_S22_SWARM_FOOT_CRASH_DESC:
The metallic fluid - the ichor - flows around the innards of the swarmer. It washes languidly over frayed wires and emergency lights, its smell clogging my nose and lungs.

UPDATE_25_TITLE: No Man's Sky version 6.3: XENO ARENA
UPDATE_25_INTRO: No Man's Sky XENO ARENA introduces simulated creature battles. Explore the universe to assemble a team of creature companions, and test their mettle in turn-based tactical combat at Holo-Arena tables.
UPDATE_25_BULLET1: BULLETPOINT Challenge other players or alien lifeforms in simulated Creature Battles!
UPDATE_25_BULLET1_SWITCH: BULLETPOINT Challenge alien lifeforms in simulated Creature Battles at the Space Anomaly or on planets.
UPDATE_25_BULLET2: BULLETPOINT Learn the strengths and weaknesses of each creature's species, size, and native climate, and refine your strategy to claim victory in any situation.
UPDATE_25_BULLET3: BULLETPOINT Discover and master hundreds of attack, defence and healing abilities for countless tactical possibilities.
UPDATE_25_BULLET4: BULLETPOINT Experiment with genetic modification to evolve your creatures, and enhance their performance in battle.
UI_PB_GENE_ACCESS_SUB: Level up and improve companion stats
UI_PB_GENES_LEVEL_POP:
Exposure to battles in the Holo-Arena will slowly mutate a companion.

Each level of mutation allows an individual gene to be edited, levelling up the companion's combat performance.
UI_PB_GENES_ROGUE_POP:
Exposure to battles in the Holo-Arena will slowly mutate a companion.

Each level of mutation allows an individual gene to be edited, levelling up the companion's combat performance.

Once a creature reaches its maximum genetic potential, further edits can be made to change the creature's available moves.
UI_PB_GENES_SPEED_DESC:
Editing this gene will improve this creature's agility, improving their chances to dodge incoming attacks. In a battle, the creature with the higher agility stat will move first.

Note: smaller creatures have a higher inherent agility.

Available edits: %NUM%. Progress to next edit: %PROGRESS%%.
UI_PB_GENES_STRENGTH_DESC:
Editing this gene will improve this creature's health, improving their chances of survival in the Holo-Arena.

Note: larger creatures have higher inherent health.

Available edits: %NUM%. Progress to next edit: %PROGRESS%%.
UI_PB_GENES_COMBAT_DESC:
Editing this gene will improve this creature's combat ability, increasing the power of their abilities. Improvements include damage, healing strength, buff duration, and more.

Available edits: %NUM%. Progress to next edit: %PROGRESS%%.

A specialised treat laced with gene-manipulating retroviruses, capable of evolving the battle abilities of a companion.

Feeding this to your tamed creatures will instantly unlock part of their genetic potential.

UI_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_DESC: The lifeform regards me with bulging eyes, oddly magnified by the curve of their tank-head.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_LANG2: Is that...? Oh! A companion register? Are you a collector?Please, let me see!
UI_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT2_DESC: The Traveller pores over the data. The crustacean-like growth in their tank bobs up and down.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT2_LANG:
This will do. It will do! A beginning.
NEUTRALBut manners! Introductions! Hello! I am Oceanus.A collector. A strategist! A Traveller, now settled. You can usually find me here, by this Holo-Arena.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT2_LANG_ALT:
Astounding! Such variety. And look at this one... what an unusual creature! A fine collection.
NEUTRALBut manners! Introductions! Hello! I am Oceanus.A fellow collector. A strategist! A Traveller, now settled. You can usually find me here, by this Holo-Arena.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT2_LANG2: It is exciting to meet a new challenger! Shall we play? A game of tactics. Your companions against mine.
UI_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT2_OPT_C: Ask if the creatures will be harmed
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT2_B_LANG:
Turn by turn, we command our collection. A clash of claws, fangs, tentacles, mandibles! Choose each command thoughtfully. When all my creatures are exhausted, you have won!
Each life, each creature, is unique. Some creatures have advantages against others. A broader collection gives broader options. Use your curiosity! Play, experiment!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT2_C_LANG: Oh, no! The Holo-Arena is a safe simulation. Your collection will learn, but they cannot be hurt.
UI_PB_TUT_OBJ2: Compete in a Creature Battle at a Holo-Arena
UI_PB_TUT_OBJ2_TIP:
Initiate battle at a Holo-Arena on the Space Anomaly.

Choose up to 3 creatures from your Companion Register or pick from a selection of simulated creatures to complete your battle team.
Use the different abilities your creatures possess to gain the upper-hand in battle!
Creatures from different biomes may be stronger or weaker than their opponent. Switch which creature is actively battling if it seems to be at a disadvantage!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_A_LANG_GEN: Wonderful game! You give me much to consider!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_A_LANG_WIN: You have learnt so quickly! I accept my defeat. For now!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_A_LANG_LOSS: The win is mine! This time. More play will mean more understanding!
UI_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_A_DESC: Oceanus's eyes shimmer in their liquid face. They seem thrilled by the challenge of battle, already calculating strategies for next time.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_A_LANG2: Take this treat. It is for your creatures. It is not for you. Do not eat it!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_A_RES: The pellet will modify the fabric of a creature. Their battle possibilities will expand, grow stronger!
UI_PB_TUT_OBJ3_TIP:
Experiment with genetic modification to evolve your creatures, and enhance their performance in battle.
Modify how they may behave in battle, increase essential stats and change which abilities they know.

Interact with a companion to feed it a retroviral pellet, then mutate a gene PET_GENE in your companion's Genetic Profile. PET_LVLUP
Open the Companion Register from the Quick Menu (QUICK_MENU).
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_B_LANG:
Did your creature enjoy the pellet? Did it... let me... ah, yes! An important gene. An interesting choice.
The Arena League encourages gene-tinkering. Retroviral pellets are sometimes presented to winners. It is all part of the game!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_B_RES_A: A faction of collectors. Intergalactic. Everywhere! Collecting brings its own satisfaction, but if medals motivate you, the Arena League offers them to the exceptional.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_B_RES_B: There are many more! Beyond Nada and Polo's home. Travellers play here, but my most challenging opponent was a Korvax in Calypso. It took me several iterations to defeat them!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_B_END: You may wish to read more about the Arena League? It is open to all!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_C_LANG: I see potential in you, stranger-collector. When you have practiced some more, would you play me again? I get so bored! I love to play, but not many can keep up with me.
UI_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_C_DESC: Oceanus sighs, their face blurred by bubbles. Then suddenlypositive they brighten.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_C_LANG2: Oh! Here. Please! Take this. This member of the Arena League has been looking for an opponent.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_TUT_C_LANG_RES:
If you best this opponent, more invitations will flow! Play! Strategise! Collect! Ascend!
The highest-ranking champions play in space stations. Once you have bested a champion, could we play again? I can barely wait!
UI_PB_TUT_OBJ4_TIP:
Learn more about the Arena League from Iteration: Oceanus.

UI_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_RDY_OSD: SLASH INCOMING MESSAGE SLASH  FREQUENCY : SPACE ANOMALY SLASH
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_RDY_LANG_1: Stranger-collector. Your creatures are drawing attention from the Arena League! I am eager to see what you have learnt. Please, can we play? You know where to find me!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_LANG_1: Hello! Shall we play? I will not hold back!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_LANG_2: Would you like to play? I long for a challenge!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_LANG_3: Play me? I am feeling sharp!
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_LANG_4: I could not be more excited to see you! Let us play? A serious match?
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_LANG_5: Let us battle? To the best of our ability!
UI_NEXUSGT_PB_EASY_LANG2: Shall we play again? More casually?
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_RET_1: I am still tired from our battle! Shall we play again? More casually?
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_RET_2: Shall we play again? A lighter game?
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_RET_3: I think I could play again today! But less intensely, please?
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_RET_4: I would like another game! But let us play gently?
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_RET_5: Another? For you, yes, but I cannot repeat our earlier pace!
UI_NEXUSGT_PB_DAILY_WAIT_DESC: The Traveller is completely absorbed in their datapad, flicking through a detailed-looking register of fauna. They do not notice my presence.
FTH_NEXUSGT_PB_INVITE_LANG_1:
A win against a champion? Congratulations! I see the beginnings of a collector-enthusiast!
Here, another challenger invite. Play! Strategise! Collect! Ascend!
FTH_NEXUSGT_LANG: It is quieter here than outside. The best place for focus! Outside is distracting. Disappointing.
UI_NEXUSGT_DESC: Oceanus is silent for a moment, bubbling quietly to themself.
FTH_NEXUSGT_LANG2: Polo promised others like me. And here, I have found you!

PET_GUILD_DESC:
United by an enthusiasm for all things zoological and sharing a keen competitive streak, members of the Arena League roam the galaxy seeking new life to tame, nurture and train.

Members can be found at Holo-Arenas on planets and Space Stations challenging one another to prove which of them has raised the most powerful, well-trained Companions in simulated battles between their creatures. They are always accepting of new challengers, though Travellers will have to prove themselves before they can expect to take on the toughest competitors.
UI_MEDAL_DESC_PB_D_NEXUS:
Each day Iteration: Oceanus hosts a unique Holo-Arena battle. Their battle team for that day is consistent for all Travellers.

Find Oceanus aboard the Space Anomaly at their personal Holo-Arena.

Iteration: Oceanus expects challengers to have deep knowledge of their Companion's strengths, weaknesses and genetic profile. 
Be prepared for a challenging battle.

UI_MEDAL_DESC_BOSS_WINS:
System Champions watch for any up-and-coming Holo-Arena competitors in their system. Claim enough victories in a system and they will invite you to battle them.

These battles are especially tough. Chances of success are improved by highly-trained companions and strong understanding of which affinities will be effective against creatures from the champion's system.
UI_MEDAL_DESC_PB_WINS:
Seek out Holo-Arenas on planets and Space Stations throughout the galaxy. 

Alien lifeforms competing at Holo-Arenas will train creatures from planets in their own system. Experienced players will form a battle team of creatures with affinities that are strong against the affinities that are found on a planet or in a system.

Considering the relative strengths of different affinities will give you a competitive edge in battle.

Your companion's hereditary traits have a minor influence on how they behave in a Holo-Arena battle.

During battles your creature may perform some actions autonomously, according to their traits and personality. Modifying Eggs at the Egg Sequencer aboard the Space Anomaly can influence the traits of your companion's offspring.

Experiment with creatures hatched from modified eggs to see how they behave when they battle.

UI_SPEC_PB_EGG01_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

Laid by a soft-skinned crustacean, this species has evolved a synergistic relationship with Travellers, occupying the discarded shells of slain Sentinel Quadrupeds.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential to be shy and migratory.
UI_SPEC_PB_EGG02_DESC:
A metal 'egg' capsule, ready to hatch!

Part robotic, part organic, part liquid. The primitive anatomy of this creature's conscious organ belies a deep, calculating intelligence.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential to be focused and strategic.
UI_SPEC_PB_EGG03_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

It wails, sleepless.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential to be haunting and adrift.
UI_SPEC_PB_EGG04_DESC:
A metal 'egg' capsule, ready to hatch!

The shell crackles with an electronic energy; mutated by Atlantideum, neutralised by [ redacted ].

Scans indicate the being within is programmed to be tireless and gLaSs.
UI_SPEC_PB_EGG05_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

The serpentine foetus stares directly through the membrane of its egg. It watches. It waits.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential to be unblinking and slithering.

UI_SETTLE_MGR_DESC:
Assist the local population in the construction of their planetary settlement on %PLANET%. Perform key actions at the Settlement Interface or in the Overseer's Office.

As Overseer of %SETTLEMENT%, you will make key decisions, direct the construction of buildings, and resolve disputes between citizens.

A well-managed settlement will produce plenty of materials - enough that a successful Overseer may claim surplus resources each day - and most settlement buildings provide practical utility for their Overseer.

DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_03: thank you for your contribution to our settlement, prebuilt-entity. we all see your hard work.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_04: this settlement was built by autophage hands. do we require a prebuilt overseer?
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_05: i accept you as overseer, prebuilt-entity. you have showed your worth.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_06: overseer has made good construction decision. we autophage exist to build.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_07: what we have built here is special. i am glad of your contribution to this settlement.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_08: i have a design for a new settlement facility, overseer. i will bring it to your desk soon.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_09: thank you for your cooperation, overseer.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_10: this settlement is alive, overseer. we need never stop construction.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_11: ah. you are our overseer. the disruptor. our friend. welcome.
DNT_BUI_WFC_OWNED_SEC_LANG_12: hello, overseer. i believe you are worth that name. you are a builder, like us.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_02: i think i know your name. you are the disruptor. welcome to our settlement.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_03: you can see me, prebuilt visitor? please do not cause trouble.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_04: this is an autophage settlement, prebuilt-entity. please visit with respect.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_05: why are you here, prebuilt-entity? what technology sees through my protection aura?
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_06: i know you. you are the disruptor! i would welcome your contribution to our settlement.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_07: we are a hidden society, prebuilt visitor. you must be very advanced to see us.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_08: we built this settlement from salvage and from pain. please do not damage it.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_09: we return to existence to build this settlement. you are welcome if your visit is peaceful.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_10: this settlement is hidden to most. but i think you are different.
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_11: a disruptor? i did not believe you were real. do you like our settlement?
DNT_BUI_WFC_SEC_LANG_12: you are not autophage. but if you know how to build, you could still earn the friendship of this settlement.
BLD_BASIC_BUILDERS_DESC:
Reinforced Salvaged building module, precisely assembled from an unusual fusion of recycled components and Atlantideum crystal.

Conforms to Universal Building Standards 2.3b, ensuring maximum compatibility with other prefab structures. Rapid grid snapping allows for quick assembly of custom shelter layouts.
BLD_B_CANOPY_WALL0_DESC: A canopy constructed from salvaged scrap. Can be affixed to structures to provide shade and embellishment.
BLD_B_WATERTOWER_DESC: An enigmatic crystal-processing device. Details of its function are unknown.
BLD_B_ANTENNA_DESC: A simple crystal-based receiver, for isolating sensitive communications from the wider network.
BLD_B_WALLHANGING_DESC: Heavyweight cables, repurposed as a wall decoration.
BLD_B_PALLET_BRICK_DESC: A pile of monitors in various states of repair.
BLD_B_LARGETRYE0_DESC: A large cog, salvaged from oversized machinery.
BLD_B_CARRIAGEWHEEL_DESC: A large spool of cable, salvaged from oversized machinery.
BLD_B_SCISSORLIFT_DESC: A mysterious device, seemingly designed to assemble robotic carapaces.
BLD_B_STREETLAMP0_DESC: A tall Atlantideum-powered street lamp, providing bright illumination.
BLD_B_SAIL_DESC: A simple crystal-based transmitter, for isolating sensitive communications from the wider network.

UI_GUIDE_BODY_BIGGS:
Corvettes are a completely bespoke class of starship - assembled piece by piece - with a traversable, furnished interior. These habitable ships are constructed in a similar fashion to planetary bases, and can be fitted out internally with living areas such as nutrition units and bunk beds.

Excavate Corvette modules from salvage containers found buried on some worlds. Scan planets with the starship scanner to detect buried salvageable scrap. Modules determine the aesthetics of the ship, and many modules also enhance specific ship stats, such as damage potential or shield strength.

Begin Corvette creation at a Corvette Workshop, found aboard Space Stations by the large landing pads near the station entrance tunnel. A number of basic modules can also be purchased from the Workshop.

Select finalise to complete a Corvette design, or exit the Workshop to resume it later.

Once a Corvette's structure is finalised, you can add internal decorations by stepping inside the ship and accessing the Build Menu with BUILD_MENU. The structure of a finalised Corvette can be also modified at the Corvette Workshop at any time.
UI_GUIDE_BODY_BIGGS_ALT:
Corvettes are a completely bespoke class of starship - assembled piece by piece - with a traversable, furnished interior. These habitable ships are constructed in a similar fashion to planetary bases, and can be fitted out internally with living areas such as nutrition units and bunk beds.

Excavate Corvette modules from salvage containers found buried on some worlds. Scan planets with the starship scanner to detect buried salvageable scrap. Modules determine the aesthetics of the ship, and many modules also enhance specific ship stats, such as damage potential or shield strength.

Begin Corvette creation at a Corvette Workshop, found aboard Space Stations by the large landing pads near the station entrance tunnel. A number of basic modules can also be purchased from the Workshop.

Select purchase to finalise a Corvette design, or save it to continue later. The cost UNITS of the final fabrication step will be determined by the size and complexity of the ship.

Once a Corvette's structure is finalised, you can add internal decorations by stepping inside the ship and accessing the Build Menu with BUILD_MENU. The structure of a finalised Corvette can be also modified at the Corvette Workshop at any time.

A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

The creature inside snuffles at the inside of its egg, curious about the world beyond.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential for a ferocious personality.
UI_TWIT_PET_22_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

The creature inside wriggles its chubby limbs, patiently waiting to be hatched.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential for a loyal personality.

A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

The weight inside this egg shifts constantly, as though the creature within is bouncing energetically.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential to be an adventurous companion, curious to explore planets beyond its frozen homeworld.
UI_TWIT_PET_24_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

The insect within snaps its mandibles, ferocious before even seeing another entity.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential to be a fierce hunter, defeating prey and rival creatures with powerful aggression.
UI_TWIT_PET_25_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

The creature inside wriggles and flexes its fluffy toes, yearning to feel soil between them.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential for a protective disposition, brimming with affection for its Traveller companion.
UI_TWIT_PET_26_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

The creature inside flexes its hefty torso.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential for a dutiful disposition; a faithful and hard-working companion.
UI_TWIT_PET_27_DESC:
A living, fertile egg, ready to hatch!

Large ears flap against the membrane of the egg, curiously listening to the world outside.

Scans indicate the being within has the genetic potential for a loyal and affectionate companion.

UI_HAUL_TUT_DESC: The Colossus and a Gravitino Coil are key pieces of equipment for any scrap-hunter. Collect, sort and process industrial waste to clean planets and extract recycled resources.

UI_HAUL_TUT_OBJ2_TIP:

Magnetised objects can be launched from the Generator with ATTACK, or gently released with ALTATTACK.

UI_HAUL_TUT_OBJ3_TIP:

UI_HAUL_TUT_OBJ4_TIP:

Assess your haul at a Waste Processing Plant. Park the loaded Colossus on the valuation scale and operate the Control Panel to automatically recycle collected material.

Collect special waste containers for additional rewards. Manually sort waste into individual processors for maximum resource recovery.

EXPED_15_INTRO:
No Man's Sky AQUARIUS invites you down to the water to relax, catch fish, and share tall tales...

Featuring a brand-new fishing system, hundreds of fish to track and collect, new customisation options, the community-wide Aquarius Expedition, and more!
EXPED_15_BULLET1: BULLETPOINT Catch, collect and catalogue a vast array of fish!
EXPED_15_BULLET2: BULLETPOINT Explore different habitats and craft unique bait to track down each new catch.
EXPED_15_BULLET3: BULLETPOINT Deploy the Exo-Skiff and fish in comfort, whatever the weather.
EXPED_15_BULLET4: BULLETPOINT Join the community on a laid-back fishing expedition and earn exclusive nautical customisation options.
EXPED_15_OUTRO:
Hello Games has been hard at work to improve and expand No Man's Sky. We hope you enjoy. :)

More will follow...
UI_JELLYBOSS_BAR_TIP: Defeat the Guardian to calm the boiling seas
UI_QUICK_MENU_SKIFF_NO_WATER: Cannot Summon :: Must deploy on water
UI_QUICK_MENU_NO_SKIFF: No Exo-Skiff interface installed in Exosuit
UI_FISH_SKIFF_DESC:
A deployable static platform, allowing the user to comfortably survey the seas in any weather. As well as providing a steady and easily accessible fishing spot, the Exo-Skiff also features abundant Cold Storage, granting additional space to store your catch. 

Summon the Exo-Skiff to any suitable body of water using the Quick Menu (QUICK_MENU).
UI_FISHLASER_DESC:
A versatile piece of angling equipment, enabling the user to fish in a variety of water conditions.

Access the fishing rig by pressing CYCLEWEAPON and cast your line into a body of water with ATTACK. With a fish hooked, press and hold ATTACK to haul in your catch.
BLD_SEAHARVESTER_DESC:
An autonomous fishing device, designed for long-term deployment in a wide-range of water conditions.

Once activated, the system will lure and trap any nearby aquatic creatures and store them for later retrieval.
BLD_SEAHARVESTER_DESC_ALT:
An autonomous fishing device, designed for long-term deployment in a wide-range of water conditions. Return later to collect trapped fish.

Trap cycle: IN PROGRESS
UI_FISH_ALL_LEG_S_DESC: "A voice like honey from a mouth of mucus."
UI_FISH_ALL_LEG_M_DESC: "Its tentacles that glitter like wisps of golden hair, but sting with the fire of thousand suns."
UI_FISH_ALL_LEG_L_DESC: "Territorial, ancient, furious to be caught. The king of the sea."
UI_FISH_ALL_LEG_XL_DESC: "A true titan of the depths. Nothing compares for sheer mass."
UI_FISH_LUSH_LEG_S_DESC: "A creature of dreams, only visible where the light refracts through its soft, perfect jelly."
UI_FISH_LUSH_LEG_M_DESC: "When hunting, can dissolve into a thin dark cloud, impossible to track, impossible to see coming..."
UI_FISH_LUSH_LEG_L_DESC: "A powerful, muscular body and teeth like razors, these gentle giants protect smaller creatures from predators."
UI_FISH_LUSH_LEG_XL_DESC: "The old man of the sea; scarred, blinded, still swimming on..."
UI_FISH_HOT_LEG_S_DESC: "Its glittering shell is practically unbreakable, a material of pure perfection."
UI_FISH_HOT_LEG_M_DESC: "Impossible to see with mortal eyes as it flashes through the water under boiling, cloudless skies."
UI_FISH_HOT_LEG_L_DESC: "A dark cloud follows this creature, and dreams of doom await all those who touch it."
UI_FISH_HOT_LEG_XL_DESC: "Heart of stone and fins of iron, this creature lives on where all else falters."
UI_FISH_COLD_LEG_S_DESC: "A living snowflake: frozen solid yet still alive, its tentacles a fractal recursion."
UI_FISH_COLD_LEG_M_DESC: "A name only spoken in whispers, its pale body a illusion that flickers beneath the moonlit waves."
UI_FISH_COLD_LEG_L_DESC: "A heart that beats but once a hour, a heart that sees faster life spawn and die, spawn and die, spawn and die..."
UI_FISH_COLD_LEG_XL_DESC: "None would believe the scale of this beast: its colossal shell, its enormous slimy foot. None, except those who have seen it..."
UI_FISH_RAD_LEG_S_DESC: "A thousand eyes erupt from its soft flesh: a never-ending cycle of rising, blinking, sinking, and re-emergence."
UI_FISH_RAD_LEG_M_DESC: "Its wings beat slowly as it sails though the poisoned seas, a drifter with no place of rest, no end to their journey."
UI_FISH_RAD_LEG_L_DESC: "A pale blue glow surrounds it as it drifts through the water - a warning to all those who would come too close..."
UI_FISH_RAD_LEG_XL_DESC: "Polymorphic, twisting, always in motion; its body a constant whirr of shifting forms and ripping teeth."
UI_FISH_TOX_LEG_S_DESC: "Its perfect crystalline form glistens with a emerald light that changes the soul of all those whose eyes fall upon it."
UI_FISH_TOX_LEG_M_DESC: "A true error of the deep; its hungry bite corrupts your blood, filling your body with a spurting corrosive bile."
UI_FISH_TOX_LEG_L_DESC: "Robbed of flesh and stripped of colour by acid seas, the bonefish swims on regardless."
UI_FISH_TOX_LEG_XL_DESC: "Seemingly weak and fragile at the surface, these giant jaws have swallowed alive many an unwary soul who ventured into their abyssal home..."
UI_FISH_DUST_LEG_S_DESC: "A delicate creature, a fragment of the past that lives on in the water."
UI_FISH_DUST_LEG_M_DESC: "The many-mouths arise from the darkness of the ocean; the many-mouths hunger for their home in the sand..."
UI_FISH_DUST_LEG_L_DESC: "A relic of another age, a fusion of life and stone that refuses to die."
UI_FISH_DUST_LEG_XL_DESC: "The apex of marine predation, a perfect killing machine. Beware."
UI_FISH_ODD_LEG_S_DESC: "Listen to these words: Do not allow this egg to hatch. Cast it back into the sea."
UI_FISH_ODD_LEG_M_DESC: "Shell and claw of perfect crystal, eyestalks aglow with purple rage; a being displaced from another reality and cast here as crab."
UI_FISH_ODD_LEG_L_DESC: "Its song resonates across time and space, calling to its home in the endless black above. One day, it will rise and return to its home among the stars."
UI_FISH_ODD_LEG_XL_DESC: "On the surface or below the waves, the vessel hungers, the vessel feeds..."
